en: The overhead closure of a room.
The upper limit of an object or action.

ceiling.ety: From Middle English celing (“paneling; (bed) cover or hanging”), from celen (“to cover or panel walls”) (from Old French celer (“to conceal”)) + -ing (gerund-forming suffix). By surface analysis, ceil + -ing.

ex.en: The device is attached fast to the ceiling.
ex.ja: その装置は天井にしっかりと固定されている。

ex.en: A fly can walk on the ceiling.
ex.ja: ハエは天井を歩くことができる。

ex.en: Down came the ceiling and the dog went away.
ex.ja: 天井が落ちてきていぬが逃げていった。

note.ja: ceil（板を張る）+ -ing。ラテン語 caelum（空・天）とされる。「天井」→「上限」。

en: A small fruit, usually red, black or yellow, with a smooth hard seed and a short hard stem.
Prunus subg. Cerasus, trees or shrubs that bear cherries.
Containing or having the taste of cherries.
Of a bright red color; cherry red.

cherry.ety: From Middle English chery, cherie, chirie, from Anglo-Norman cherise (mistaken as a plural) and Old English ċiris, ċirse (“cherry”), from Proto-West Germanic *kirsijā, from Vulgar Latin ceresia, derived from Late Latin ceresium, cerasium, from Ancient Greek κεράσιον (kerásion, “cherry fruit”), from κερασός (kerasós, “bird cherry”), and ultimately possibly of Anatolian origin (the intervocalic σ suggests a pre-Greek origin for the word). Doublet of cerise, Giresun, and kirsch.

ex.en: There's an old cherry tree in the garden.
ex.ja: 庭に古い桜の木が一本あります。

ex.en: There's a dead body under the cherry tree!
ex.ja: 桜の樹の下には屍体が埋まっている！

ex.en: There are dead bodies under the cherry trees!
ex.ja: 桜の樹の下には屍体が埋まっている！

note.ja: 古フランス語 cherise から。英語では s を複数語尾と考えて取り去った。

en: A moderate, but uncomfortable and penetrating coldness.
A sudden penetrating sense of cold, especially one that causes a brief trembling nerve response through the body; the trembling response …
Moderately cold or chilly.
Unwelcoming; not cordial.
To lower the temperature of something; to cool.
To become cold.

chill.ety: From Middle English chele, chile, from Old English ċiele, ċele (“cold; coldness”), from Proto-West Germanic *kali, from Proto-Germanic *kaliz, from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“to be cold”). Closely related with Dutch kil. Also akin to cool, cold, gel, and congeal, which see.

ex.en: Cold rain makes me chilled to the bone.
ex.ja: 冷たい雨がわたしの身体を骨まで凍えさせる。

ex.en: I want to chill the wine more.
ex.ja: ワインをもっと冷やしたいんだ。

ex.en: I feel chilled to the bone today.
ex.ja: 今日は底冷えのする日だ。

note.ja: 古英語 ciele（冷たさ）から。cold と同じ語根。「冷え」→（口語）chill out（くつろぐ）。

ex.en: Support vector machines are supervised learning models used for classification and regression analysis.
ex.ja: サポートベクターマシンとは、教師あり学習モデルであり、判別分析や回帰分析に用いられる。

note.ja: classify（分類する）+ -cation。「分類」。class と同じ。

en: Information which may lead one to a certain point or conclusion.
An object or a kind of indication which may be used as evidence.
To provide with a clue.
To provide someone with information which they lack (often used with "in" or "up").

clue.ety:
Variant of clew (“a ball of thread or yarn”), from Middle English clew, clewe, clowe, clue, clwe, clyw, clywe, from Old English clēowen, clīewen, clīowen, clīwen, clȳwe, clȳwen (“ball, sphere; skein”), from Proto-West Germanic *kliuwīn (“ball, clump”), from Proto-Germanic *kliuwīną, *klewô (“bale, ball, clump, mass”), from Proto-Indo-European *glew- (“to ball up, clump together; lump, swelling”). Sense evolution with reference to the one which the mythical Theseus used to guide him out of the Minotaur's labyrinth. More at clew.
Cognates
Cognate with Cimbrian khnaul (“ball of yarn”), Dutch kluw

ex.en: Have you found any clues to the problem?
ex.ja: その問題の解決に何か手がかりは見付かりましたか。

ex.en: Do you have any clue to the mystery?
ex.ja: その謎を解く何か手がかりがありますか。

ex.en: Don't ask me, I really have no clue.
ex.ja: 私に聞かないで。本当にわからないから。

note.ja: clew（糸玉）の変化形。ギリシャ神話でテセウスが糸玉をたどって迷宮から出たことから「手がかり」。

en: To break apart and fall down suddenly; to cave in.
To cease to function due to a sudden breakdown; to fail suddenly and completely.
The act of collapsing.
Constant function, one-valued function (in automata theory) (in particular application causing a reset).

collapse.ety: From Latin collāpsus (past participle of collābor).

ex.en: If you don't take a vacation, you'll collapse.
ex.ja: 休暇を取らないと、体が参ってしまいますよ。

ex.en: The old bridge is in danger of collapse.
ex.ja: その古い橋は今にも崩れ落ちそうだ。

ex.en: The house collapsed under the weight of snow.
ex.ja: 雪の重さで家がつぶれた。

note.ja: ラテン語 collapsus（崩れ落ちた）から。com + labi（滑り落ちる）。「崩壊する」。lapse と同じ。

en: An enclosure within which workers, prisoners, or soldiers are confined.
An enclosure for secure storage.
Composed of elements; not simple.
Dealing with numbers of various denominations of quantity, or with processes more complex than the simple process.
To form (a resulting mixture) by combining different elements, ingredients, or parts; to mingle with something else.
To settle by agreeing on less than the claim, or on different terms than those stipulated.

compound.ety: Possibly from Malay kampong, kampung (“group of buildings, village”), via Dutch or Portuguese, altered under the influence of Etymology 2. Doublet of kampung.

ex.en: The plants manufacture complex chemical compounds.
ex.ja: 工場では複雑な化学化合物を製造している。

ex.en: There are lots of four-character compound words in Japanese, huh?
ex.ja: 日本語は四字熟語って結構あるね。

ex.en: The pain from the compound fracture was almost intolerable.
ex.ja: 複雑骨折の痛みはほとんど耐え難かった。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pound（= pon 置く）。一緒に置いたもの →「混合物・化合物・複合の」。

en: Alert, awake; with one's mental faculties active.
Aware of one's own existence; aware of one's own awareness.
The part of the mind that is aware of itself; the consciousness.

conscious.ety: First use appears c. 1573 in the sense of "aware of wrongdoing".https://web.archive.org/web/20220714064352/https://www.lexico.com/definition/conscious From Latin cōnscius (“conscious, conscious of guilt”), itself from con- (a form of com- (“together”)) + scīre (“to know”) + -us.

ex.en: He was not conscious of my presence here.
ex.ja: 彼は私がここにいることに気づいていなかった。

ex.en: He was not conscious of his own mistake.
ex.ja: 彼は自分の間違いに気付いていなかった。

ex.en: He was not conscious of his weak point.
ex.ja: 彼は自分の弱点に気づいていなかった。

note.ja: con（共に）+ sci（知る）+ ous。自分と共に知っている →「意識している・気づいている」。

en: Following, in succession, without interruption.
Having some logical sequence.
A sequence of notes or chords that results from repeated shifts in pitch of the same interval.
A linguistic form that implies or describes an event that follows temporally from another.

consecutive.ety: From French consécutif, from Medieval Latin cōnsecūtīvus, from Latin cōnsecūtus (“followed up”), from Latin cōnsequor (“to travel”).

ex.en: Steel output set a record for two consecutive years.
ex.ja: 鉄鋼生産は２年連続して最高を記録した。

ex.en: This is the fifth consecutive day of decline of stock prices.
ex.ja: 今日で５日連続の株価下落だ。

ex.en: Stock prices declined for five consecutive days.
ex.ja: 株価は５日連続して下がった。

note.ja: con（共に）+ secu（続く）+ tive。続いて起こる →「連続した」。

en: A style of dress, including garments, accessories and hairstyle, especially as characteristic of a particular country, period or people.
An outfit or a disguise worn as fancy dress etc.
To dress or adorn with a costume or appropriate garb.

costume.ety:
Borrowed from French costume, from Italian costume, from Latin consuētūdō (“custom, habit”). Doublet of consuetude, custom, and kastom.
Verb circa 1802, perhaps modelled on French costumer.

ex.en: She designed beautiful costumes for the movie.
ex.ja: 彼女はその映画のために美しい衣装をデザインした。

ex.en: The costumes were red, pink, blue, and so forth.
ex.ja: 服は赤、ピンク、青色などであった。

ex.en: Tom and Mary went shopping together for their costumes.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは一緒に衣装を買いに行った。

note.ja: イタリア語 costume（習慣・装い）から。ラテン語 consuetudo（習慣）。custom と同じ語源。

en: to give one's time, focus one's efforts, commit oneself, etc. entirely for, on, or to a certain matter; to consecrate.
to consign over; to doom

devote.ety: Borrowed from Latin dēvōtus, past participle of Latin dēvoveō (“dedicate by a vow, sacrifice oneself, promise solemnly”). Doublet of devow; see also devout. Displaced native Middle English ēstful, from Old English ēstful.

ex.en: The old lady was devoted to her dog.
ex.ja: その老婦人は自分の犬をたいへんかわいがった。

ex.en: I want to devote my life to education.
ex.ja: 私は人生を教育に捧げたい。

ex.en: He devoted himself to music in those days.
ex.ja: 当時彼は音楽に没頭していた。

note.ja: ラテン語 devovere ＝ de + vovere（誓う）。「誓ってささげる」。vow、vote と同じ。

en: To govern, rule or control by superior authority or power.
To exert an overwhelming guiding influence over something or someone.
Dominant.
The late period of the Roman Empire, following the principate, during which the emperor's rule became more explicitly autocratic and rema…

dominate.ety: Borrowed from Latin dominātus, perfect active participle of dominor (“to rule, have dominion”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from dominus (“lord, master”) + -or (verb-forming suffix).

ex.en: He dominates his family and makes all the decisions.
ex.ja: 彼はその家を支配し、すべての決断をする。

ex.en: She dominates her husband.
ex.ja: 彼女は夫を尻に敷いている。

ex.en: Her heart was dominated by ambition.
ex.ja: 彼女の心は野心の虜になっていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 dominus（主人）から。dom + inate。主人として振る舞う →「支配する・優位を占める」。

en: Having no end.
Extending indefinitely.

endless.ety: From Middle English endeles, from Old English endelēas (“endless”), from Proto-Germanic *andijalausaz (“endless”), equivalent to end + -less.

ex.en: It will only mean an endless debate.
ex.ja: それは結局水掛け論だ。

ex.en: An endless flow of tears fell from her eyes.
ex.ja: 彼女の目から涙がとめどなく流れていた。

ex.en: He has an endless store of good jokes.
ex.ja: 彼はおもしろい笑い話を無限に知っている。

note.ja: end（終わり）+ -less。「終わりのない」。

en: To observe carefully or critically to learn about someone or something.
To check the health or condition of something or someone.
An act of examining.

examine.ety: From Middle English examinen, examenen, from Old French examiner, from Latin exāmināre.

ex.en: The police are examining the car accident now.
ex.ja: 警察は今その交通事故を調べている。

ex.en: You should have a doctor examine your condition.
ex.ja: 健康状態を医者に診てもらったほうがいい。

ex.en: I am to examine the papers once more.
ex.ja: 私はもう一度その書類を調べなければいけません。

note.ja: ラテン語 examinare（量る）から。examen（天秤の針）。「調べる」。exam と同じ。

en: To be supported by a fluid of greater density (than the object).
To be supported by a liquid of greater density, such that part (of the object or substance) remains above the surface.
A buoyant device used to support something in water or another liquid.
A mass of timber or boards fastened together, and conveyed down a stream by the current; a raft.

float.ety: From Middle English floten, from Old English flotian (“to float”), from Proto-West Germanic *flotōn, from Proto-Germanic *flutōną (“to float”), from Proto-Indo-European *plewd-, *plew- (“to float, swim, fly”). Compare flow, fleet.

ex.en: The boat was broken by the floating ice.
ex.ja: その船は漂っている氷によって壊された。

ex.en: A ball is floating down the river.
ex.ja: ボールが川を流れている。

ex.en: Then she was floating on her back.
ex.ja: それから彼女はあおむけに浮いていた。

note.ja: 古英語 flotian から。flow、fleet と同系。「浮く」→ パレードの「山車」。

en: Food waste material of any kind.
Useless or disposable material; waste material of any kind.
bad, crap, shitty

garbage.ety:
From late Middle English garbage (“the offal of a fowl, giblets, kitchen waste”, originally “refuse, what is purged away”), from Anglo-Norman, from Old French garber (“to refine, make neat or clean”), of Germanic origin, from Frankish *garwijan (“to make ready”).
Akin to Old High German garawan (“to prepare, make ready”), Old English ġearwian (“to make ready, adorn”). More at garb, yare, gear

ex.en: The garbage-can gave off a bad smell.
ex.ja: そのごみ箱は悪臭を放っていた。

ex.en: The garbage is giving off a terrible smell.
ex.ja: そのゴミはひどいにおいを出している。

ex.en: Our garbage is collected three times a week.
ex.ja: 私たちのゴミは週３回収集されます。

note.ja: 中英語 garbage（鳥の内臓）から。語源ははっきりしない。（米）「ごみ」。

en: The first section of the Christian New Testament scripture, comprising the books of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, concerned with the birt…
An account of those aspects of Jesus' life, generally written during the first several centuries of the Common Era.
To instruct in, declare, or communicate the gospel; to evangelise.

gospel.ety: From Middle English gospel, gospell, godspel, godspell, goddspell, from Old English godspell (“gospel”), corresponding to God + spell (“talk, tale, story”), literally “the message of God”, believed to be an alteration of earlier *gōdspell (literally “good news”), used to translate ecclesiastical Latin bona annūntiātiō, itself a translation of Ecclesiastical Latin ēvangelium / Ancient Greek εὐαγγέλιον (euangélion, “evangel”, literally “good news”) (English evangel). Compare Old Saxon gōdspel and godspell (“gospel”), Old High German and Middle High German gotspel (“gospel”), Icelandic guðspjall

ex.en: They spread the Gospel all over the world.
ex.ja: 彼らはキリストの福音を全世界に広めた。

ex.en: What he says is gospel.
ex.ja: 彼の言うことは絶対正しい。

note.ja: 古英語 gōdspel ＝ gōd（よい）+ spel（知らせ）。ギリシャ語 euangelion（よい知らせ）の翻訳。

en: The harvested seeds of various grass food crops, especially wheat, maize, rye, barley, and rice.
Similar seeds from any food crop, e.g., buckwheat, amaranth, quinoa.
To feed grain to.
To make granular; to form into grains.

From Middle English greyn, grayn, grein, from Old French grain, grein, from Latin grānum (“seed”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵr̥h₂nóm (“grain”). Doublet of corn, gram, granum, and grao.

ex.en: We shouldn't waste even one grain of rice.
ex.ja: 私たちは米一粒でさえ無駄にしてはいけません。

ex.en: They have plenty of grain in store.
ex.ja: 彼らは大量の穀物を蓄えている。

ex.en: It goes against the grain with me.
ex.ja: 僕はそれが気にいらない。

note.ja: ラテン語 granum（穀粒）から。「穀物・粒」→ 木の「木目」。granite、grenade と同じ語源。

en: A rectangular array of squares or rectangles of equal size, such as in a crossword puzzle.
A tiling of the plane with regular polygons; a honeycomb.
To mark with a grid.
To assign a reference grid to.

grid.ety: Back-formation or clipping of griddle or gridiron.

note.ja: gridiron（焼き網）からの逆成。「格子」→ 送電の「網」。

en: The act of identifying (i.e., which one, which thing).
The combination of identifying (which one, which thing) and validating the identity (proving or confirming it); identifying and authentic…

ex.en: May I see two pieces of identification?
ex.ja: 身分証明書を二枚拝見できますか。

ex.en: Do you have your student identification card?
ex.ja: 学生証は持ってる？

ex.en: May I see your identification?
ex.ja: 身分証明書をお願いします。

note.ja: identify（特定する）+ -cation。「身分証明・識別」。ID はその略。

ja: ひざ（座ったときの太ももの上）

en: The loose part of a coat; the lower part of a garment that plays loosely; a skirt; an apron.
An edge; a border; a hem, as of cloth.
To enfold; to hold as in one's lap; to cherish.
To rest or recline in someone's lap, or as in a lap.

lap.ety: From Middle English lappe, from Old English læppa (“skirt or flap of a garment”), from Proto-West Germanic *lappō, from Proto-Germanic *lappô (“cloth; rag”), of uncertain origin, possibly Proto-Indo-European *leb- (“to hang loosely”). Cognate with Dutch lap (“cloth; rag”), German Lappen (“cloth; lobe; flap”), Icelandic leppur (“rag; patch”).

ex.en: The dog has lapped up the milk.
ex.ja: 犬がミルクをなめてしまった。

ex.en: She was brought up in the lap of luxury.
ex.ja: 彼女は贅沢にそだてられた。

ex.en: Tom lives in the lap of luxury.
ex.ja: トムは贅沢三昧に暮らしている。

note.ja: 「ひざ」は古英語 læppa（衣服の垂れ）から。座ったときの太ももの上。競技の「1周」は「重ねる・包む」の意味の別語。

en: A rapid transit rail transport system, or a train in such systems, generally underground and serving a metropolitan area.
An urban rapid transit rail transport system, normally with lighter track and light trains (i.e. an S-Bahn or similar), or a train in suc…
metropolitan

metro.ety: From French métro, clipping of métropolitain (from Ancient Greek μήτηρ (mḗtēr, “mother”) + πόλις (pólis, “city”)), as in the Chemin de fer métropolitain, an early name for the Paris Métro. This name was a direct translation of "Metropolitan Railway", which was the original name of the earliest part of the London Underground, constructed in 1863.

ex.en: There is a metro in Kazan.
ex.ja: カザンに地下鉄がある。

ex.en: It takes twenty minutes on the metro to get to the city centre.
ex.ja: 都心まで、地下鉄で20分です。

note.ja: フランス語 métropolitain（大都市の）の短縮。パリの地下鉄 Métro から。ギリシャ語 mētēr（母）+ polis（都市）。

en: A bishop empowered to oversee other bishops; an archbishop.
The inhabitant of a metropolis.
Pertaining to the see or province of a metropolitan.
Of, or pertaining to, a metropolis or other large urban settlement.

ex.en: He centered his business on the metropolitan area.
ex.ja: 彼はその商売を都心に集中した。

ex.en: How high is the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Office Building?
ex.ja: 東京都庁ビルの高さはどのくらいありますか。

ex.en: The flu struck the metropolitan area.
ex.ja: インフルエンザが都市部で猛威を振るった。

note.ja: metr（母）+ o + polit（都市）+ an。母なる都市（metropolis 首都）の →「大都市の・首都圏の」。

en: The act of mixing.
Something produced by mixing.

mixture.ety: From Middle English, borrowed from Old French misture, from Latin mixtūra (“a mixing”), from mixtus, perfect passive participle of misceō (“mix”); compare mix.

ex.en: Every opinion is a mixture of truth and mistakes.
ex.ja: どんな意見も真実と誤りの混合だ。

ex.en: You can't make a mixture of oil and water.
ex.ja: 油と水はいっしょに混ぜ合わせることはできない。

ex.en: Mixture of the three primary colors creates black.
ex.ja: 三原色を混合すると黒色ができる。

note.ja: mix（混ぜる）+ -ture。「混合物」。

en: Having received a nomination.

ex.en: The Prime Minister nominated him as Foreign Minister.
ex.ja: 総理大臣は彼を外務大臣に任命した。

ex.en: I have been nominated for the chairman.
ex.ja: 私は議長に任命された。

ex.en: The President nominated him to be Secretary of State.
ex.ja: 大統領は彼を国務長官に指名した。

note.ja: nominate（指名する）+ -ed。ラテン語 nomen（名前）。「名前を挙げられた」。

en: A deciduous tree with distinctive deeply lobed leaves, acorns, and notably strong wood, typically of England and northeastern North Ameri…
The wood of the oak.
Having a rich brown color, like that of oak wood.
Made of oak wood or timber.
To expose to oak in order for the oak to impart its flavors.

oak.ety:
Inherited from Middle English ake, hok, oek, ok, oke, from Old English aac, āc, ǣċ, from Proto-West Germanic *aik, from Proto-Germanic *aiks (“oak”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eyǵ- (“oak”).

ex.en: The oak tree remained standing after the storm.
ex.ja: あらしのあとカシの木は倒れずに残った。

ex.en: These oaks are over a hundred years old.
ex.ja: これらの樫の木は樹齢100年以上です。

ex.en: Are there oak trees on the hill?
ex.ja: 丘の上にかしの木がはえていますか。

note.ja: 古英語 āc から。「オーク（カシ・ナラ類）」。

Having the supreme executive and legislative power resting with a cabinet of ministers chosen from, and responsible to a parliament.

ex.ja: 国会討論の放送を聞きましたか。

en: An official document granting an appointment, privilege, or right, or some property or title; letters patent.
A grant of a monopoly over the manufacture, sale, and use of goods.
To (successfully) register (a new invention) with a government agency to obtain the sole privilege of its manufacture, sale, and use for …
To obtain (over a piece of real property) a specific grant of ownership.
Conspicuous; open; unconcealed.
Of flour: fine, and consisting mostly of the inner part of the endosperm of the grain from which it is milled.

patent.ety:
The noun is derived from Middle English patent (“document granting an office, property, right, title, etc.; document granting permission, licence; papal indulgence, pardon”) [and other forms], which is either:
* a clipping of lettre patent, lettres patente, lettres patentes [and other forms]; or
* directly from Anglo-Norman and Middle French patente (modern French patent), a clipping of Anglo-Norman lettres patentes, Middle French lettres patentes, lettre patente, and Old French patentes lettres (“document granting an office, privilege, right, etc., or making a decree”) (compare Late Latin pat

ex.en: A patent right is an important property right.
ex.ja: 特許権は重要な財産権である。

ex.en: Hans sold the patent to a company.
ex.ja: ハンスさんが会社へ特許権を売りました。

ex.en: Where is the Tokyo patent office?
ex.ja: 東京特許許可局はどこですか？

note.ja: ラテン語 patens（開いている）から。patere（開いている）。letters patent（公開の書状）→「特許」。「明白な」も同じ。

en: The organisation, identification and interpretation of sensory information.
Conscious understanding of something.

perception.ety: From Middle English percepcioun, from Middle French percepcion, from Latin perceptiō (“a receiving or collecting, perception, comprehension”), from perceptus (“perceived, observed”), perfect passive participle of percipiō (“to perceive, observe”); see perceive.

ex.en: I'm afraid my depth perception is very poor.
ex.ja: 遠近感がとぼしいのです。

ex.en: The perception of beauty is a moral test.
ex.ja: 美の認識は倫理の検査となり得る。

ex.en: The simple perception of natural forms is a delight.
ex.ja: 自然の姿を見るだけで、それは一つの喜びである。

note.ja: per（完全に）+ cept（つかむ）+ ion。しっかりつかみ取ること →「知覚・認識」。perceive（知覚する）。

en: A practitioner of physic, i.e. a specialist in internal medicine, especially as opposed to a surgeon; a practitioner who treats with medi…
A medical doctor trained in human medicine.

physician.ety: From Middle English fisicien, from Old French fisicïen (“physician”) (modern French physicien (“physicist”)), from fisique (“art of healing”), from Latin physica (“natural science”), from Ancient Greek φυσική ἐπιστήμη (phusikḗ epistḗmē, “knowledge of nature”), from φυσικός (phusikós, “pertaining to nature”). Displaced native Middle English læche, leche, archaic English leech (“physician”). Morphologically physic + -ian.

ex.en: He is the physician I talked about yesterday.
ex.ja: 彼はきのう私が話題にした医者です。

ex.en: A six-figure income isn't uncommon for physicians.
ex.ja: 医者なら６桁の収入は珍しくない。

ex.en: The physician prescribed his patient some medicine.
ex.ja: 医者は患者に薬を処方した。

note.ja: physic（医術）+ -ian。ギリシャ語 physis（自然）。自然を学んだ人 →「医師」。physics と同じ。

en: To move, pass, or go forward or onward; to advance; to carry on.
To pass from one point, topic, or stage, to another.

proceed.ety: From Middle English proceden, from Old French proceder, from Latin prōcēdō (“to go forth, go forward, advance”), from prō (“forth”) + cēdō (“to go”); see cede.

ex.en: He proceeded in the face of danger.
ex.ja: 彼は危険に直面しても進んでいった。

ex.en: He proceeded to the next question.
ex.ja: 次の問題にとりかかった。

ex.en: Let's proceed with the items on the agenda.
ex.ja: 議題に上っている項目の議論を続けましょう。

note.ja: pro（前へ）+ ceed（進む）。前へ進む →「進む・続行する」。

en: A learner at a school under the supervision of a teacher.
One who studies under supervision of a renowned expert in their field.

pupil.ety: From Middle English pupille, from Anglo-Norman pupille (“orphan”), from Latin pūpillus (“orphan, minor”), variant of pūpulus (“little boy”), from pūpus (“child, boy”).

ex.en: How many pupils are there in your school?
ex.ja: あなたの学校には何人の生徒がいますか。

ex.en: How many pupils are there in your class?
ex.ja: あなたのクラスには何人の生徒がいますか。

ex.en: The pupils are bound down by the rules.
ex.ja: 生徒たちは規制で縛りつけられている。

note.ja: ラテン語 pupillus（幼い子）・pupilla（小さな人形）から。「生徒」と、のぞき込むと小さな人影が映ることから「瞳孔」。

en: To reestablish, or bring back into existence.
To bring back to good condition from a state of decay or ruin.
The act of recovering data or a system from a backup.

restore.ety: From Middle English restoren, from Old French restorer, from Latin rēstaurāre. By surface analysis, re- + store.

ex.en: How on earth can we restore our youth?
ex.ja: 一体どうしたら若さが取り戻せるのだろう。

ex.en: It was suggested that the tower be restored.
ex.ja: その塔を復元してはどうかと提案された。

ex.en: After decades of civil war, order was restored.
ex.ja: 数十年の内戦の後に秩序が回復した。

note.ja: ラテン語 restaurare（再建する）から。re + staurare（立てる）。「元通りにする」。restaurant と同じ。

en: A firearm fired from the shoulder; improved range and accuracy is provided by a long, rifled barrel.
An artillery piece with a rifled barrel.
To quickly search through many items (such as papers, the contents of a drawer, a pile of clothing).
To commit robbery or theft.

rifle.ety: Originally short for “rifled gun”, referring to the spiral grooves inside the barrel. From Middle English riflen (“to rob, plunder, search through”), from Old French rifler (“to lightly scratch, scrape off, plunder”), from Old High German riffilōn (compare German riffeln (“to score, make grooves in, ripple”), archaic Dutch rijfelen (“to scrape”), Old English rifelan, riflian (“to wrinkle”)), frequentative of Proto-Germanic *rīfaną (compare Old Norse rífa (“to tear, break”)). More at rive.

ex.en: He carried a rifle on his shoulder.
ex.ja: 彼は肩に銃を担いだ。

ex.en: A rifle shot broke the peace of the early morning.
ex.ja: ライフルの発射音が早朝の静けさを破った。

ex.en: The soldier refused to fire his rifle at the enemy.
ex.ja: その兵士は敵に向けてライフル銃を発射する事を拒否した。

note.ja: 「ライフル銃」は rifle（銃身にらせん状の溝を刻む）から。フランス語 rifler（ひっかく）。「くまなく探す」も同じ語源。

en: A competitor (person, team, company, etc.) with the same goal as another, or striving to attain the same thing. Defeating a rival may be …
Someone or something with similar claims of quality or distinction as another.
Having the same pretensions or claims; standing in competition for superiority.
To oppose or compete with.
To be equal to, or match, or to surpass another.

rival.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin rīvālis (literally “person using the same stream as another”). By surface analysis, Latin rīvus + -al.

ex.en: Two rival parties are essential to good democratic government.
ex.ja: 健全な民主主義には対立した二等が不可欠だ。

ex.en: We lost out to our rival in price competition.
ex.ja: 私たちはライバルに価格競争で敗れた。

ex.en: I find a good rival in him.
ex.ja: 彼は相手にとって不足はない。

note.ja: ラテン語 rivalis（同じ川を使う人）から。rivus（小川）。水を奪い合う隣人 →「競争相手」。river、derive と同系。

en: A person who moves, on foot, at a fast pace, especially an athlete.
Any entrant, person or animal (especially a horse), for a race or any competition; a candidate for an election.

runner.ety:
From Middle English rennere, rynner, urnare, equivalent to run + -er. Cognate with Old Norse rennari (“runner; messenger”). Displaced earlier Middle English runel (“runner”), from Old English rynel (“runner”; also “messenger, courier”).
((botany) a long stolon sent by a plant): Compare typologically Russian побе́г (pobég) (akin to бежа́ть (bežátʹ)).

ex.en: Some runners drink water as they are running.
ex.ja: 走者の中には走りながら水を飲む者もいる。

ex.en: Brazil finished runners-up in the 1998 World Cup.
ex.ja: 1998年のワールドカップでは、ブラジルは準優勝に終わった。

ex.en: Before the race, the runners have to warm up.
ex.ja: レースの前にランナーはウォーミングアップしなければなりません。

note.ja: run（走る）+ -er。「走者」。

en: In a sad manner; sorrowfully.
Unfortunately, sad to say.

sadly.ety: From Middle English sadly; equivalent to sad + -ly.

ex.en: Sadly, my cat has gone away somewhere.
ex.ja: 悲しいことに私の猫はどこかへいってしまった。

ex.en: Sadly, his dream didn't come true.
ex.ja: 悲しいことに彼の夢は実現しなかった。

ex.en: "He used to love me," she answered sadly.
ex.ja: 以前は愛してくれたのだけれど。と彼女は悲しそうに答えた。

note.ja: sad（悲しい）+ -ly。「悲しそうに」→ 文全体を修飾して「残念ながら」。

en: The extent to which something matters; importance
Meaning.

significance.ety: Inherited from Middle English significaunce, from Middle French significance, from Old French significance, from Latin significantia. Doublet of signifiance.

ex.en: Your thoughts are of no significance at all.
ex.ja: 君の考えなどはどうだっていいことだ。

ex.en: It has no absolute and universal significance.
ex.ja: それには絶対的で普遍的な意味はない。

ex.en: Recently he has come to realize the significance of married life.
ex.ja: 最近彼は結婚生活の意味がわかるようになった。

note.ja: significant（重要な）+ -ance。「重要性・意味」。sign と同じ。

en: A metallic salt derived from a fatty acid, commonly used in cleaning products.
Some other substance, often a detergent or another surfactant, able to mix with both oil and water, used for cleaning.
To apply soap to in washing.
To cover, lather, or in any other manner treat with soap, often as a prank.

soap.ety:

Proto-West Germanic *saipā

From Middle English sope, sape, from Old English sāpe (“soap, salve”), from Proto-West Germanic *saipā, from Proto-Germanic *saipǭ, from Proto-Indo-European *seyb-, *seyp- (“to pour out, drip, trickle, strain”).
Cognate with Scots saip, sape (“soap”), Saterland Frisian Seepe (“soap”), West Frisian sjippe (“soap”), Dutch zeep (“soap”), German Low German Seep (“soap”), German Seife (“soap”), Danish sæbe (“soap”), Swedish såpa (“soap”), Norwegian Bokmål såp

ex.en: Wash your hands with a bar of soap.
ex.ja: 石鹸で手を洗いなさい。

ex.en: She used up a cake of soap.
ex.ja: 彼女は石鹸を一個使ってしまった。

ex.en: She used up a bar of soap.
ex.ja: 彼女は石鹸を一個使ってしまった。

note.ja: 古英語 sāpe から。ゲルマン語起源。soap opera は石けん会社が昼のドラマのスポンサーだったことから。

en: A fine, gentle, dispersed mist of liquid.
Something resembling a spray of liquid.
To project a liquid in a dispersive manner toward something.
To project in a dispersive manner.

spray.ety:
From Middle Dutch sprāien, sprayen, spraeyen (“to spray, sprinkle, spread”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *sprēwijaną (“to spray, sprinkle”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)per- (“to sow, scatter”).
Cognate with Middle High German spræjen, spræwen (“to squirt, spray, dust, splash, straw”), Danish dialectal språe (“to open up, burst forth”), Swedish dialectal språ (“to sprout, shoot forth, burst”), Norwegian dialectal spra, spræ (“to splash, splatter, spout, burst forth”), Dutch sproeien (“to spray, sprinkle”), German sprühen (“to spray, sparkle”).

ex.en: The waves sprayed the rocks with water.
ex.ja: 波は岩に水しぶきをかけた。

ex.en: They are spraying the fruit trees.
ex.ja: 彼らは果樹に農薬を散布している。

ex.en: She sprayed pesticide on the flowers.
ex.ja: 彼女は花に殺虫剤を振りまいた。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 sprayen（まき散らす）から。「しぶき」→「スプレー・吹きかける」。

en: Of, relating to, or having structure.
Involving the mechanics of construction.
Structural steel, used in construction.

ex.en: The structural formula for water is H-O-H.
ex.ja: 水の構造式は H-O-H である。

note.ja: structure（構造）+ -al。「構造の」。

en: A group or train of attendants, servants etc.; a retinue.
A connected series or succession of objects; a number of things used or classed together.

suite.ety: Borrowed from Middle French suite. See also the doublet suit.

ex.en: She had the hotel suite to herself.
ex.ja: 彼女はホテルのスイートルームを独り占めにした。

ex.en: I'd like a suite.
ex.ja: スイートルームをお願いします。

ex.en: This suite is three times larger than my condominium.
ex.ja: このスイートルームは私の住んでいるマンションの三倍の広さだ。

note.ja: フランス語 suite（続くもの）から。「ひと続き」→「（ホテルの）続き部屋・一式・組曲」。suit、sequence と同じ語源。

en: Of or pertaining to the tropics, the equatorial region between 23 degrees north and 23 degrees south.
From, or similar to, a hot, humid climate.
A tropical plant.

ex.ja: どんなトロピカルドリンクがありますか。

ex.en: This is a tropical storm. It'll be over soon.
ex.ja: 通り雨だからすぐ止むよ。

ex.en: It seemed that they were interested in tropical fish.
ex.ja: 彼らは熱帯魚に興味があるらしかった。

note.ja: tropic（回帰線）+ -al。ギリシャ語 tropos（回転）。「熱帯の」。tropics と同じ。

en: Relating to Ukraine or its people or language.
A person from Ukraine or of Ukrainian descent.

Ukrainian.ety: From Ukraine + -ian (suffix meaning ‘from; like; related to’, forming adjectives; or ‘one belonging to, from, like, or relating to’, forming nouns).

ex.en: The Ukrainian conflict is raising prices throughout the world.
ex.ja: ウクライナでの紛争が、世界中の物価を引き上げてしまっている。

ex.en: Ukrainian girls are the prettiest in the world.
ex.ja: 世界で一番美しい女はウクライナの女だ。

ex.en: I don't speak Ukrainian.
ex.ja: ウクライナ語は話せません。

note.ja: Ukraine + -ian。スラブ語 ukraina（辺境・国）とされる。

en: Not needed or necessary.
Done in addition to requirements; unrequired.

unnecessary.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *né
Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Germanic *un-
Proto-West Germanic *un-
Old English un-
Middle English un-
English un-
English necessary
English unnecessary
From un- + necessary.

ex.en: It is very important to tell the necessary from the unnecessary.
ex.ja: 必要なものと必要でないものを見分けることがきわめて重要である。

ex.en: If two people are in agreement, one of them is unnecessary.
ex.ja: もし二人の人が常に同じ意見を持っていたら、そのうちの一人は必要ない。

ex.en: We reduced the price by eliminating unnecessary functions.
ex.ja: ムダな機能を省いて安くしました。

note.ja: un（否定）+ necessary（必要な）。ラテン語 necesse（避けられない）、ne + cedere（退く）。

en: A poetic form with regular meter and a fixed rhyme scheme.
Poetic form in general.
To tell in verse, or poetry.
to educate about, to teach about.

verse.ety: From Middle English vers, from a mixture of Old English fers and Old French vers; both from Latin versus (“a line in writing, and in poetry a verse; (originally) row, furrow”), from vertō (“to turn around”).

ex.en: A collection of her verses has just been published.
ex.ja: 彼女の詩集が出版されたところだ。

ex.en: He wrote several plays in verse.
ex.ja: 彼はいくつかの戯曲を韻文で書いた。

ex.en: Give me chapter and verse.
ex.ja: 一部始終を聞かせてくれ。

note.ja: ラテン語 versus（向きを変えること）から。vers（向ける）。鋤を返すように行を折り返すもの →「詩・韻文・（歌の）節」。

en: The winner in a fight or contest.

victor.ety: Inherited from Middle English victour, victor, from Anglo-Norman victor, Latin victor (“conqueror”). Doublet of Victor.

note.ja: ラテン語 victor（勝者）から。vincere（勝つ）。victory、convince と同じ vic。

en: The yield of grapes or wine from a vineyard or district during one season.
Wine, especially high-quality, identified as to year and vineyard or district of origin.
Of or relating to a vintage, or to wine identified by a specific vintage.
Having an enduring appeal; high-quality.
To harvest (grapes).
To make (wine) from grapes.

vintage.ety: From Middle English vendage, vyndage, from Anglo-Norman vendenge, from Old French vendage, vendenge (cognate with French vendange), from Latin vindēmia (“a gathering of grapes, vintage”), from vīnum (“wine”) + dēmō (“take off or away, remove”), from de (“of; from, away from”) + emō (“take”).

ex.en: Is this a vintage car?
ex.ja: 旧車ですか。

ex.en: What vintage is this wine?
ex.ja: このワインって、何年ものなの？

note.ja: 古フランス語 vendage（ぶどうの収穫）から。ラテン語 vinum + demere（取る）。「ぶどうの収穫年」→「年代物の・極上の」。wine と同じ。

ja: エーカー（約4047平方メートル）

en: An English unit of land area (symbol: a. or ac.) originally denoting a day's ploughing for a yoke of oxen, now standardized as 4,840 squa…
An area of 10,240 square yards or 4 quarters.

From Middle English acre, aker, from Old English æcer (“field where crops are grown”), from Proto-West Germanic *akr, from Proto-Germanic *akraz (“field”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵros (“field”). Doublet of agriculture.
Cognate with Scots acre, aker, acker (“acre, field, arable land”), North Frisian ecir (“field, a measure of land”), West Frisian eker (“field”), Dutch akker (“field”), German Acker (“field, acre”), Norwegia

ex.en: I bought an eight-acre farm for my retirement.
ex.ja: 私は退職後のために８エーカーの農場を買った。

ex.en: They sell land by the acre.
ex.ja: 土地はエーカー単位で売っています。

ex.en: The field measures more than 300 acres.
ex.ja: 畑は面積が３００エーカー以上ある。

note.ja: 古英語 æcer（畑）から。ラテン語 ager（agriculture）と同じ祖先。1日で耕せる面積とされた。

en: To make suitable; to make to correspond; to fit or suit.
To fit by alteration; to modify or remodel for a different purpose; to adjust.
Adapted; fit; suited; suitable; apt.

ex.ja: 君は様々な状況に適応しなければならない。

ex.en: Some plants cannot adapt themselves to the cold.
ex.ja: ある種の植物は寒さに順応できない。

ex.en: Children quickly adapt themselves to their new life.
ex.ja: 子供たちはすぐに新しい生活に順応する。

note.ja: ラテン語 adaptare ＝ ad + aptare（合わせる）。「ぴったり合わせる」→「適応する」。apt と同じ。

en: The act of adopting.
The state of being adopted; the acceptance of a child of other parents as if they were one's own child.

adoption.ety: Borrowed from French adoption, from Latin adoptio, allied to adoptare (“to adopt”). Equivalent to adopt + -ion.

note.ja: adopt（採用する）+ -ion。「採用・養子縁組」。

en: Lacking a name; not named, for example an animal not assigned to any species .
Without any name acknowledged of a person responsible.

anonymous.ety: Borrowed into English around 1600 from Late Latin anonymus, from Ancient Greek ᾰ̓νώνῠμος (ănṓnŭmos, “without name”), from ᾰ̓ν- (ăn-, “un-”) with ὄνῠμᾰ (ónŭmă), Aeolic and Doric dialectal form of ὄνομᾰ (ónomă, “name”). English equivalent an- + -onymous.

ex.en: I want to remain anonymous in this.
ex.ja: この件では名前を出したくない。

ex.en: We got an anonymous call.
ex.ja: 匿名の電話があったんです。

ex.en: The poem was composed by an anonymous author.
ex.ja: その詩は無名の著者が詠んだ。

Relating to or characteristic of art or artists.

ex.ja: 庭園の芸術的な美しさが素晴らしいです。

ex.en: It is the most artistic picture I have ever taken.
ex.ja: それは、私がこれまでとったもっとも芸術的な写真です。

note.ja: artist（芸術家）+ -ic。「芸術的な」。

en: The act of attending; the state of being present; presence.
A tally or listing of the persons present.

attendance.ety: From Middle English attendance, from Old French atendance, from atendre (“to attend, listen”).

ex.en: Regular attendance is important in a foreign language class.
ex.ja: 外国語の授業ではきちんと出席する事が大切です。

ex.en: Regular attendance is required in that class.
ex.ja: その授業には規則正しく出席することが必要だ。

ex.en: We request your attendance at the meeting.
ex.ja: ぜひ会に出席をお願いします。

note.ja: at（〜へ）+ tend（伸ばす）+ ance。〜へ足を伸ばすこと →「出席・出席者数」。

en: The art or science of making and flying aircraft.
Flying, operating, or operation of aircraft.

aviation.ety: Borrowed from French aviation, derived from Latin avis (“bird”). By surface analysis, avi- + -ation.

ex.en: The aviation expert analyzed the statistics in detail.
ex.ja: その航空専門家は統計を詳細に分析した。

ex.en: The world's aviation industry is growing increasingly worried about crashes.
ex.ja: 世界の航空産業は墜落事故についての懸念を募らせている。

ex.en: Compared to fifty years ago, today's aviation technology has made great progress.
ex.ja: ５０年前と比べると、今日の航空技術はずいぶん発達したものだ。

note.ja: フランス語 aviation から。ラテン語 avis（鳥）。「鳥のように飛ぶこと」→「航空」。

en: A round (cylindrical) vessel, such as a cask, of greater length than breadth, and bulging in the middle, made of staves bound with hoops,…
Such a cask of a certain size, holding one-eighth of what a tun holds. (See a diagram comparing cask sizes.)
To put or to pack in a barrel or barrels.
To move quickly or in an uncontrolled manner.

barrel.ety:
Etymology tree
Old French barilbor.
Middle English barel
English barrel
From Middle English barel, from Anglo-Norman baril, Old French baril, bareil (“barrel”), of uncertain origin. An attempt to link baril to Old French barre (“bar, bolt”) (compare Medieval Latin barra (“bar, rod”)) via assumed Vulgar Latin *barrīculum meets the phonological requirement, but fails to connect the word semantically. The alternative connection to Frankish *baril, *beril or Gothic *𐌱𐌴𐍂𐌹𐌻𐍃 (*bērils, “container for transport”), from Proto-Germanic *barilaz, *bērilaz (“barrel, jug, container”), from Proto-Indo-Europ

ex.en: Middle Eastern oil prices jumped by five dollars per barrel.
ex.ja: 中東の石油価格は１バレル当たり５ドルほど跳ね上がりました。

ex.en: The GOP accused the Democrats of pork barrel politics.
ex.ja: 共和党は民主党の地方人気とり補助金政策を非難しました。

ex.en: One rotten apple spoils the barrel.
ex.ja: 腐ったリンゴが１つあるとたる全体がだめになる。

note.ja: 古フランス語 baril から。語源ははっきりしない。「たる」→ 石油の単位、筒状の「銃身」。

en: Much loved, dearly loved.
Someone who is loved; something that is loved.

beloved.ety: From Middle English beloved, biloved, equivalent to belove + -ed.

ex.en: He couldn't possibly part with his beloved dog.
ex.ja: 彼は大事な犬をとうてい手放すことはできなかった。

ex.en: His wife died leaving behind their two beloved children.
ex.ja: 彼の妻は二人の愛の結晶を残して死んだ。

ex.en: He died leaving his beloved children behind.
ex.ja: 彼は愛する子供たちを残して死んだ。

note.ja: be（強意）+ loved（愛された）。「最愛の」。

en: A movie theatre, a movie house.
Films collectively.

cinema.ety:

Borrowed from French cinéma, clipping of cinématographe (term coined by the Lumière brothers in the 1890s), from Ancient Greek κίνημα (kínēma, “movement”) + γράφω (gráphō, “write, record”). Compare German Kino (“cinema”), ultimately from the same Greek source.

ex.en: She went to the cinema the other day.
ex.ja: 先日彼女は映画に行った。

ex.en: I went to the cinema with my brother.
ex.ja: 兄と映画に行きました。

ex.en: He often goes to the cinema with her.
ex.ja: 彼はよく彼女と一緒に映画に行く。

note.ja: cinematograph の短縮。ギリシャ語 kinēma（動き）+ graph。「動きを記録するもの」。kinetic と同じ。

en: Of or pertaining to a colony.
Of or pertaining to a period when a country or territory was a colony.
A person from a country that is or was controlled by another.
A house that is built in a style reminiscent of the period of the colonization of New England.

colonial.ety:

ex.en: He dates the custom from the colonial days.
ex.ja: その習慣を彼は植民地時代から始まると推定している。

ex.en: During the colonial period, the place was rather exclusionary, admitting only foreign residents.
ex.ja: 植民地時代には、外国人居住者に限定されたかなり排他的な場所でした。

note.ja: colony（植民地）+ -al。「植民地の」。

en: An act of complying.
The state of being compliant.

From comply + -ance.

ex.en: We are building your house in compliance with your wishes.
ex.ja: 私達はご希望通りにお宅を建てております。

ja: 正反対（on the contrary 逆に）

en: Opposite; in an opposite direction; in opposition; adverse.
Opposed; contradictory; inconsistent.
Contrarily
The opposite.
One of a pair of propositions that cannot both be simultaneously true, though they may both be false.

contrary.ety: From Middle English contrarie, compare French contraire, from Old French contraire, from Latin contrārius (“opposite, opposed, contrary”), from contrā (“against”).

ex.en: This is quite contrary to what I want.
ex.ja: これは私の欲しいものとまるっきり反対だ。

ex.en: My point of view is contrary to yours.
ex.ja: 私の見解はあなたの見解とは反対である。

ex.en: I had a contrary opinion to the plan.
ex.ja: 私はその計画に対して反対の意見を持っていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 contrarius（反対の）から。contra（反対に）。「反対の」→ on the contrary（逆に）。

en: An item of furniture, often upholstered, for the comfortable seating of more than one person; a sofa.
A bed, a resting-place.
To lie down; to recline (upon a couch or other place of repose).
To bend the body, as in reverence, pain, labor, etc.; to stoop; to crouch.

couch.ety: From Middle English couche, cowche, from Old French couche, from the verb (see below). Doublet of cwtch.

ex.en: The TV remote control is under the couch.
ex.ja: テレビのリモコンがソファーの下にある。

ex.en: She's going to sit on the yellow couch.
ex.ja: 彼女は黄色のソファに座ります。

ex.en: No problem. I can sleep on the couch.
ex.ja: 構わないよ。ソファーで寝れるし。

note.ja: 古フランス語 couche（寝床）から。coucher（横たえる）。「寝いす・ソファー」。

en: A violent collision or compression; a crash; destruction; ruin.
Violent pressure, as of a moving crowd.
To press between two hard objects; to squeeze so as to alter the natural shape or integrity, or to force together into a mass.
To reduce to fine particles by pounding or grinding.

crush.ety:
From Middle English cruschen (“to crush, smash, squeeze, squash”), from Old French croissir (“to crush”), from Late Latin *crusciō (“to crush”), from Frankish *krustijan (“to crush, squeeze, squash”), from Proto-Germanic *kreustaną (“to crush, grind, strike, smash”).
Cognate with Middle Low German tôkrosten (“to crush, shatter”), Swedish krysta (“to squeeze”), Danish kryste (“to squash”), Icelandic kreista (“to squeeze, squash”), Faroese kroysta (“to squeeze”), Gothic 𐌺𐍂𐌹𐌿𐍃𐍄𐌰𐌽 (kriustan, “to gnash”). Akin also to Middle Dutch crosen (“to bruise, crush”), Middle Low German krossen, krö̂sen, tôk

ex.en: I used to have a little crush on you.
ex.ja: 君のことが少し好きだったよ。

ex.en: It's true that I had a crush on her.
ex.ja: 彼女にぞっこんだったのは本当だよ。

ex.en: He crushed the sheet of paper up into a ball.
ex.ja: 彼はその紙を握りつぶして丸めた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 croissir（砕く）から。「押しつぶす」→ 心がつぶれるほどの「片思い」。

en: A structure placed across a flowing body of water to stop the flow or part of the flow, generally for purposes such as retaining or diver…
The water reservoir resulting from placing such a structure.
To block the flow of water.

dam.ety: From Middle English dam, from Old English *damm, from Proto-West Germanic *damm, from Proto-Germanic *dammaz.

ex.en: There was a water mill below the dam.
ex.ja: ダムの下流に水車小屋があった。

ex.en: This dam supplies us with water and electricity.
ex.ja: このダムは私たちに水と電力を供給している。

ex.en: Is there much water in the dam?
ex.ja: そのダムには水がたくさんありますか。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 dam（土手）から。「ダム・せき止める」。Amsterdam（アムステル川のダム）の dam。

en: Of a quantity, to become smaller.
To make (a quantity) smaller.
An amount by which a quantity decreases or is decreased.
A reduction in the number of stitches, usually accomplished by suspending the stitch to be decreased from another existing stitch or by k…

decrease.ety: From Middle English decresen, alteration of discresen, from Anglo-Norman, Old French descreistre (French: décroître), from Latin decrescere.

ex.en: Travel by train has been on the decrease.
ex.ja: 列車の旅は減る傾向にある。

ex.en: The number of students is decreasing year by year.
ex.ja: 学生の数は年々減少している。

ex.en: The number of members decreased to five.
ex.ja: 会員は５人に減った。

note.ja: de（下へ）+ crescere（成長する）。「下向きに育つ」→「減少する」。increase の対。

en: Diabetes mellitus; any of a group of metabolic diseases whereby a person (or other animal) has high blood sugar due to an inability to pr…
Diabetes insipidus; any condition characterized by excessive or incontinent urine, now specifically as caused by impaired production of, …

diabetes.ety: From Latin diabētēs (“siphon”), from Ancient Greek διαβήτης (diabḗtēs), from Ancient Greek διαβαίνω (diabaínō, “to pass through”).

ex.en: Does anyone in your close family have diabetes?
ex.ja: 近親者の中に、糖尿病の方はいらっしゃいますか？

ex.en: Tom got diabetes from drinking too many sports drinks.
ex.ja: トムはスポーツドリンクの飲みすぎで糖尿病になったらしい。

ex.en: He was watchful for any sign of diabetes.
ex.ja: 彼は糖尿病のどんな兆しにも注意していた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 diabētēs（サイフォン・通り抜けるもの）から。dia + bainein（行く）。大量の尿が体を通り抜けることから。

en: A kind; a stylistic category or sort, especially of literature or other artworks.
To assign or conform to a genre, to make genre-specific.

genre.ety: Unadapted borrowing from French genre, from Old French gen(d)re, borrowed from Latin genere. Doublet of gender and genus.

ex.en: The historical novel was a very popular genre.
ex.ja: 歴史小説はとても人気の高いジャンルでした。

ex.en: The "city pop" genre is now garnering attention across the world.
ex.ja: 今、世界で『シティ・ポップ』が注目を集めています。

note.ja: フランス語 genre（種類）から。ラテン語 genus と同じ gen。→「（芸術の）ジャンル・種類」。

en: Tender and amiable; of a considerate or kindly disposition.
Soft and mild rather than hard or severe.
To become gentle.
To break; to tame; to domesticate.
A maggot used as bait by anglers.
A trained falcon, or falcon-gentil.

gentle.ety: From Middle English gentil (“courteous, noble”), from Old French gentil (“high-born, noble”), from Latin gentilis (“of the same family or clan”), from gens (“[Roman] clan”). Doublet of gentile, genteel, and jaunty.

ex.en: At first sight, he seemed kind and gentle.
ex.ja: 一見、彼は親切で優しい人のようだった。

ex.en: I was taken in by his gentle manner.
ex.ja: 彼の親切な態度にすっかり騙された。

ex.en: Mary is very gentle with her baby sister.
ex.ja: メアリーはベビーシッターにとても優しい。

note.ja: ラテン語 gentilis（同じ一族の・家柄のよい）から。gen（一族）。よい家柄の →「優しい・穏やかな」。gentleman（紳士）。

en: A system of rules and principles for the structure of a language, or of languages in general.
The study of such a system.

grammar.ety: From Middle English gramere, from Old French gramaire (“classical learning”), from unattested Vulgar Latin *grammāria, an alteration of Latin grammatica, from Ancient Greek γραμματική (grammatikḗ, “skilled in writing”), from γράμμα (grámma, “line of writing”), from γράφω (gráphō, “write”), from Proto-Indo-European *gerbʰ- (“to carve, scratch”). Displaced native Old English stæfcræft; a doublet of glamour, glamoury, gramarye, and grimoire. Piecewise doublet of grammatic.

ex.en: Grammar, which I hate, is good for me.
ex.ja: 文法は、私の大嫌いなものですが、ためになります。

ex.en: Please explain the grammar of 'as may be'.
ex.ja: as may be の文法解釈を教えてください。

ex.en: I'm having a hard time with German grammar.
ex.ja: ドイツ語の文法に手こずっています。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 grammatike（文字の技術）から。gram（書かれたもの）。→「文法」。

en: To clarify something by giving, or serving as, an example or a comparison.
To provide a book or other publication with pictures, diagrams or other explanatory or decorative features.

ex.en: I will illustrate the way people use language.
ex.ja: 人々の言葉の使い方を説明しましょう。

ex.en: The teacher will illustrate how to do it.
ex.ja: 先生がそのやり方を説明するだろう。

ex.en: The chart illustrates how the body works.
ex.ja: その図は体の働きを説明している。

note.ja: ラテン語 illustrare（明るく照らす）から。in + lustrare（照らす）。「明らかにする」→「説明する・挿絵を入れる」。illustrious と同じ。

en: To design a new process or mechanism.
To create something fictional for a particular purpose.

invent.ety:
From Middle English inventen, borrowed from Old French inventer, from Latin inventus, perfect passive participle of inveniō (“come upon, meet with, find, discover”), from in (“in, on”) + veniō (“come”); see venture. Compare advent, covent, event, prevent, etc.
Displaced native Old English āþenċan (literally “to think out”).

ex.en: It is said that he also invented concrete.
ex.ja: 彼はコンクリートも発明したと言われている。

ex.en: Such a machine has not yet been invented.
ex.ja: その手のマシンはまだ発明されていない。

ex.en: All that which is invented, is true.
ex.ja: 作り事はすべて、真実だ。

note.ja: in（中へ・上に）+ vent（来る）。（考えが）頭の中に来る・行き当たる →「発明する・でっち上げる」。

en: A sweet mixture of fruit boiled with sugar and allowed to congeal. Often spread on bread or toast or used in jam tarts
A difficult situation.
To get something stuck, often (though not necessarily) in a confined space.
To brusquely force something into a space; to cram, to squeeze.

jam.ety:
First attested in the early 18th c. as a verb meaning “to press, be pressed, be wedged in”. Compare dialectal jammock (“to press, squeeze, crush into a soft mass, chew food"; also "a soft, pulpy substance”). Perhaps from Middle English chammen, champen ("to bite upon something, gnash the teeth"; whence modern champ, chomp), of uncertain origin; probably originally onomatopoeic.
The "performance" sense is first attested with regards to jazz in 1929, and its origin, though uncertain, is likely metaphorical, "something sweet made by the combination of many things", with influence from jamboree.

ex.en: We met a traffic jam on the way.
ex.ja: 途中で交通渋滞に遭った。

ex.en: There is a traffic jam on the highway.
ex.ja: 高速道路が渋滞している。

ex.en: The bus was late because of the traffic jam.
ex.ja: バスは交通渋滞のために遅れた。

note.ja: 17世紀からの語。擬音的な語とされる。「押し込む」→「渋滞」→ 果物を押しつぶした「ジャム」。

en: An interest in land granting exclusive use or occupation of real estate for a limited period; a leasehold.
An interest granting exclusive use of any thing, such as a car or boat.
To grant a lease as a landlord; to let.
To hold a lease as a tenant; to rent.

lease.ety: From Middle English *lesen, from Anglo-Norman *leser, Old French lesser, laisier (“to let, let go”), partly from Latin laxō (“to loose”) and partly from Old High German lāzan (“to let, let go, release”) (German lassen), cognate with Old English lǣtan (“to allow, let go, leave, rent”) whence let.

ex.en: Deposits on long-term leases.
ex.ja: 長期貸借契約預かり金。

note.ja: 古フランス語 lais（貸すこと）から。laissier（残す・放す）。「賃貸借契約」。release と同系。

en: An object, usually made of glass, that focuses or defocuses the light that passes through it.
A device which focuses or defocuses other waves or radiation, such as microwave radiation, electron beams, sound waves (acoustic lenses),…
To film, shoot.
To become thinner towards the edges.

lens.ety:
Etymology tree
substratebor.?
Medieval Latin lēnsbor.
English lens
Borrowed from Latin lēns (“lentil”), with Medieval Latin later taking on the sense of “lens”, a semantic loan from Arabic عَدَسَة (ʕadasa, “lentil; optic lens”); the similar shape is the common factor.

ex.en: Will you find my contact lens for me?
ex.ja: ぼくのコンタクトレンズを見つけてくれないか。

ex.en: May I have a pair of contact lenses?
ex.ja: コンタクトレンズを作っていただけますか。

ex.en: When did you start wearing contact lenses?
ex.ja: コンタクトレンズをつけ始めたのは、いつですか？

note.ja: ラテン語 lens（レンズ豆）から。形がレンズ豆に似ていることから。lentil と同じ。

en: The state of being loyal; fidelity.
Faithfulness or devotion to some person, cause or nation.

loyalty.ety: From Middle English loialte, borrowed from Old French loialte, loiauté (Modern loyauté) from loial + -té, equivalent to loyal + -ty.

ex.en: This shows his loyalty to his friends.
ex.ja: このことは友人に対する彼の誠実さを示すものだ。

ex.en: I require absolute loyalty of my employees.
ex.ja: 私は全従業員に絶対的な忠誠を求めます。

ex.en: Can I count on your loyalty?
ex.ja: 君の忠誠を当てにしてもいいかい。

note.ja: loyal（忠実な）+ -ty。古フランス語 loial、ラテン語 legalis（法にかなった）。legal と同じ語源。

en: Of, relating to, operating by, or caused by magnetism.
Having the properties of a magnet, especially the ability to draw or pull.

magnetic.ety:

English magnet

Proto-Italic *-ikos

English magnetic
From magnet + -ic.

ex.en: So there is a magnetic field around earth.
ex.ja: だから地球の周りには磁場があります。

ex.en: She has something of a magnetic force.
ex.ja: 彼女には何か磁力のようなものがある。

ex.en: But the earth's magnetic field is very weak.
ex.ja: ところが地球の磁場はごく弱いものです。

note.ja: magnet（磁石）+ -ic。ギリシャ語 Magnēs lithos（マグネシア地方の石）。「磁気の」→「人を引きつける」。

zh: 來源不明的 /来源不明的
難以理解的 /难以理解的

en: Of unknown origin.
Having unknown qualities.

mysterious.ety: From Middle English *misterius (implied in misteriusly), probably partly from Middle French mystérieux and partly from Latin mystērium + -ous. By surface analysis, mystery + -ous.

ex.en: He was suddenly attacked by a mysterious disease.
ex.ja: その子は突然わけのわからない病気に襲われた。

ex.en: There is something mysterious about the accident.
ex.ja: あの事故には何かなぞめいたものがつきまとっている。

ex.en: She has a mysterious air about her.
ex.ja: 彼女は何か神秘なところがある。

note.ja: mystery（謎）+ -ous。ギリシャ語 mystērion（秘儀）、myein（目・口を閉じる）。「謎めいた」。

en: Mental apprehension of whatever may be known, thought, or imagined; idea, concept.
A sentiment; an opinion.

notion.ety: From Latin nōtiō (“a becoming acquainted, a taking cognizance, an examination, an investigation, a conception, idea, notion”), from nōscō (“to know”). Compare French notion. See know.

ex.en: I had no notion that you were coming.
ex.ja: 君がくるとは思わなかった。

ex.en: All these notions I have long since abandoned.
ex.ja: 私はこのような考えをずっと前にすっかり捨ててしまった。

ex.en: His notions were what is called advanced.
ex.ja: 彼の考えはいわゆる進歩的なものだった。

note.ja: ラテン語 notio（知ること）から。noscere（知る）。「考え・概念」。notice、know と同じ祖先。

en: Existing as a part or portion; incomplete.
Describing a property that holds only when an algorithm terminates.
A partial derivative: a derivative with respect to one independent variable of a function in multiple variables while holding the other v…
Any of the sine waves which make up a complex tone; often an overtone or harmonic of the fundamental.
To take the partial regression coefficient.

partial.ety: From Middle English partiall, parcial, from Old French parcial (“biased or particular”), from Late Latin partiālis (“of or pertaining to a part”), from Latin pars (“part”).

ex.en: She is in partial agreement with this decision.
ex.ja: 彼女はこの決定に部分的に同意している。

ex.en: The play was only a partial success.
ex.ja: その芝居は部分的な成功しかおさめなかった。

ex.en: His business was only a partial success.
ex.ja: 彼の事業は部分的な成功をおさめたにすぎなかった。

note.ja: part（部分）+ ial。一部分の →「部分的な・不公平な（一方に偏った）」。

en: Agitation, publicity, public communication aimed at influencing an audience and furthering an agenda.
The propagation of the faith by the Catholic Church by means of missionary work etc.

ex.en: Appreciate the importance of propaganda in politics.
ex.ja: 政治における宣伝活動の重要性を認識する。

ex.en: Don't swallow that slick propaganda.
ex.ja: そのうまい宣伝に乗るな。

note.ja: ラテン語 propagare（広める）から。17世紀のカトリック教会の布教省（Congregatio de propaganda fide）から。propagate と同じ。

en: Any of the numerous members of several rodent families that usually have short limbs, a pointy snout, a long, hairless tail, and a body l…
A medium-sized rodent belonging to the genus Rattus.
To hunt or kill rats.
To betray a political party, cause or principle; to betray someone, to desert a person or thing.

rat.ety:
From Middle English raat, rat, ratt, ratte, rotte, from Old English ræt, rætt, from Proto-West Germanic *ratt, from Proto-Germanic *rattaz, *rattō (“rat”), of uncertain origin, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *Hreh₃d- (“to gnaw, scrape, scratch”). However, the rat may have been unknown in Northern Europe in antiquity, and the Proto-Germanic word may have referred to a different animal; see *rattaz for more. Attestation of this family of words begins in the 12th century.
Cognates
Cognate with North Frisian root (“rat”), Saterland Frisian Rotte (“rat”), West Frisian rôt (“rat”), Dutch rat, rot

ex.en: The rat made a hole in the wall.
ex.ja: ねずみが壁に穴をあけた。

ex.en: At last the rats came to the river.
ex.ja: とうとうねずみたちは川の所までやってきました。

ex.en: "I smell a rat", I said to him.
ex.ja: 「怪しい」僕は彼に言った。

note.ja: 古英語 ræt から。「ネズミ」→「裏切り者」。mouse より大きいものを指す。

en: The act of reflecting or the state of being reflected.
The property of a propagated wave being thrown back from a surface (such as a mirror).

reflection.ety: From Middle English refleccion, refleccioun, refleccioune, reflection, from Middle French reflection, reflexion, and its source Late Latin reflexiō, from the participle stem of reflectō. The current spelling is influenced by reflect. Equivalent to reflect + -ion.

ex.en: I'm looking at my reflection in the lake.
ex.ja: 僕は湖に映った自分の姿を見てるんです。

ex.en: She is a reflection of her mother.
ex.ja: 彼女は母親にそっくりだ。

ex.en: His bad behavior is a reflection on his common sense.
ex.ja: 行儀の悪さは彼の良識を疑わせるものだ。

note.ja: re（後ろへ）+ flect（曲げる）+ ion。曲げ返されたもの →「反射・映った姿・熟考」。

en: To find a solution to (a problem).
To reduce to simple or intelligible notions; to make clear or certain; to unravel; to explain.
Determination; will power.
A determination to do something; a fixed decision.

resolve.ety: From Middle English resolven, from Old French resolver, a learned borrowing of Latin resolvō (“loosen, thaw, melt, resolve”), equivalent to re- + solve. Piecewise doublet of re-solve.

ex.en: This liquid can be resolved into three elements.
ex.ja: この液体は３つの要素に分解できる。

ex.en: We had a hard time resolving that problem.
ex.ja: その問題を解決するのに苦労したんだよ。

ex.en: He made a resolve to stop smoking.
ex.ja: タバコをやめようと彼は決心した。

note.ja: ラテン語 resolvere ＝ re + solvere（解く）。「解きほぐす」→「解決する・決心する」。solve と同じ。

en: Of or pertaining to a revolution in government; tending to, or promoting, revolution
Of or pertaining to something that portends of great change; overthrowing a standing mindset
A revolutionist; a person who revolts.

revolutionary.ety: Compare French révolutionnaire; equivalent to revolution + -ary.

ex.en: The revolutionary council met to plan strategy.
ex.ja: 革命評議委員会は戦略の計画を立てるために集まった。

ex.en: The most radical revolutionary will become a conservative the day after the revolution.
ex.ja: 最も急進的な革命家が革命の翌日には保守になる。

ex.en: This invention is so revolutionary, it might make it into the textbooks.
ex.ja: これは、画期的な発明だから教科書に載るかもよ。

note.ja: revolution（革命）+ ary。大転換の →「革命の・画期的な」。

en: An incident or event that disgraces or damages the reputation of the persons or organization involved.
Damage to one's reputation.

scandal.ety:
From Middle French scandale (“indignation caused by misconduct or defamatory speech”), from Ecclesiastical Latin scandalum (“that on which one trips, cause of offense”, literally “stumbling block”), from Ancient Greek σκάνδαλον (skándalon, “a trap laid for an enemy, a cause of moral stumbling”), from Proto-Indo-European *skand- (“to jump”). Cognate with Latin scandō (“to climb”). First attested from Old Northern French escandle, but the modern word is a reborrowing. Doublet, via Old French esclandre, of slander.
Sense evolution from "cause of stumbling, that which causes one to sin, stumbling

ex.en: The scandal has badly damaged his clean image.
ex.ja: スキャンダルは彼の清潔なイメージを酷く傷つけた。

ex.en: I have nothing to do with the scandal.
ex.ja: 私はその汚職とは全く関係がない。

ex.en: The Prime Minister was involved in a scandal.
ex.ja: 首相はスキャンダルに巻き込まれた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 skandalon（わな・つまずきの石）から。「信仰のつまずき」→「醜聞」。slander（中傷）と同じ語源。

en: To emit or reflect light so as to glow.
To reflect light.
Brightness from a source of light.
Brightness from reflected light.

shine.ety:
From Middle English shinen, schinen (preterite schon, past participle schinen), from Old English sċīnan (“to shine, flash; be resplendent”; preterite sċān, past participle sċinen), from Proto-West Germanic *skīnan (“to shine”), from Proto-Germanic *skīnaną (“to shine”).
Cognate with Dutch schijnen, German scheinen, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål skinne, Norwegian Nynorsk and Swedish skina, Faroese and Icelandic skína.

ex.en: The game will be played rain or shine.
ex.ja: 試合は雨天決行です。

ex.en: The game will be held rain or shine.
ex.ja: 試合は晴雨を問わず行われます。

ex.en: The moon and stars were shining above us.
ex.ja: 頭上には月と星が輝いていた。

note.ja: 古英語 scīnan から。sheen（つや）と同系。「輝く」→（靴を）「磨く」。

ex.ja: 彼らは一斉に立ち上がった。

ex.en: The summit talks are to be broadcast simultaneously throughout the world.
ex.ja: 首脳会談は世界中で同時に放送される予定だ。

ex.en: Preparations for the new project are under way in both companies simultaneously.
ex.ja: 新しい計画の準備が両者で同時に進行中である。

note.ja: simultaneous（同時の）+ -ly。ラテン語 simul（同時に）。「同時に」。similar と同系。

en: To use in place of something else, with the same function.
To use X in place of Y.
A replacement or stand-in for something that achieves a similar result or purpose.
A substitute teacher.

substitute.ety: From Middle English substituten, from Latin substitutus, past participle of substituō, from sub- (“under; beneath”) + statuō (“to put up; establish”). Displaced native Old English spala (“a substitute”) and spelian (“to substitute”).

ex.en: It is impossible to substitute machines for people.
ex.ja: 機械を人の代わりにするのは不可能だ。

ex.en: It is impossible to substitute machines for people themselves.
ex.ja: 機械を人の代わりにするのは不可能だ。

ex.en: He substituted a light for the bell.
ex.ja: 彼はベルの代わりに明かりを用いた。

note.ja: sub（下に・代わりに）+ stit（立てる）+ ute。代わりに立てる →「代わり（の人・物）・代用する」。

ex.en: They will figure out the location from the surveillance footage.
ex.ja: 監視カメラの映像から位置を割り出す。

en: The military science that deals with achieving the objectives set by strategy.
The employment and ordered arrangement of forces in relation to each other.

ex.en: Nobody failed in the tactics.
ex.ja: 誰もその作戦に失敗しなかった。

ex.en: They moved the troops back in a sudden change of tactics.
ex.ja: 彼らは戦術を急に変更して軍を後退させた。

ex.en: The aide suggested a change in tactics to him.
ex.ja: 副官は戦術の変更を彼に提案した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 taktika（配置の技術）から。tassein（並べる）。軍隊の配置 →「戦術」。syntax と同じ。

en: Statements made by a witness in court.
An account of first-hand experience.

testimony.ety:
PIE word
 *tréyes
Inherited from Middle English testimonie, from Old French testimonie, from Latin testimōnium (“testimony”).

ex.en: But still you people do not accept our testimony.
ex.ja: しかし、あなた方は私たちの証を受け入れません。

ex.en: His testimony is close to the truth.
ex.ja: 彼の証言は真相に近い。

ex.en: There were points in her testimony that didn't add up.
ex.ja: 彼女の証言にはつじつまが合わない点がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 testimonium（証拠）から。testis（証人）。testify、protest と同じ。

en: Of or pertaining to Thailand.
A person living in or coming from Thailand.
A domestic cat of a particular breed descended from cats of Thailand and somewhat resembling a Siamese.

Thai.ety: Borrowed from Thai ไทย (tai). Doublet of Tai and Dai.

ex.en: He can speak Thai as well as English.
ex.ja: 彼は、英語だけでなくタイ語も話せます。

ex.en: There's a nice Thai restaurant near here.
ex.ja: 近くにおいしいタイ料理のお店があるんです。

ex.en: I'd like to try some Thai food.
ex.ja: タイ料理を食べてみたいです。

note.ja: タイ語 Thai（タイ人）から。「自由な人」の意味とされる。

en: A collection of valuable things; accumulated wealth; a stock of money, jewels, etc.
Anything greatly valued.
To consider to be precious; to value highly.
To store or stow in a safe place.

treasure.ety: Inherited from Middle English tresour, from Old French tresor (“treasury”), from Latin thēsaurus (“treasure”), from Ancient Greek θησαυρός (thēsaurós, “treasure house”). Mostly displaced native Old English goldhord (See goldhoard) and Old English ġestrēon. Doublet of thesaurus.

ex.en: It isn't known where the treasures were hidden.
ex.ja: その宝物がどこに隠されたのか誰も知らない。

ex.en: The treasure lay hidden for a long time.
ex.ja: その財宝は長い間隠されていた。

ex.en: This ball is the treasure of that boy.
ex.ja: このボールはあの男の子の宝物です。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 thēsauros（宝庫）から古フランス語を経た語。thesaurus と同じ。

en: An object, usually in the form of a statuette, cup, or shield, awarded for success in a competition or to mark a special achievement.
An object taken as a prize by a hunter, or a conqueror or belligerent, especially one that is displayed.
To adorn (someone) with trophies.
To win a trophy in a competition.

trophy.ety: From Middle French trophée, from Latin trophaeum (“a sign of victory, a monument”), tropaeum, from Ancient Greek τρόπαιον (trópaion, “monument of an enemy's defeat”), from neuter of τροπαῖος (tropaîos, “of defeat”), from τροπή (tropḗ, “a rout, a turning of an enemy”). Doublet of tropæum.

ex.en: He held the trophy up high.
ex.ja: 彼はトロフィーを高々と差し上げた。

ex.en: He held the trophy on high.
ex.ja: 彼はトロフィーを高々と差し上げた。

ex.en: She presented him with the trophy.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼にトロフィーを贈った。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 tropaion（敵が敗走した場所に立てた記念碑）から。tropē（向きを変えること）。「戦利品」→「トロフィー」。

en: The sound of a bird; any short high-pitched sound or whistle.
An entry posted on the microblogging service Twitter.
To produce a short high-pitched sound, similar to that of certain birds.
To post an entry to Twitter.
used to represent the sound of a bird twittering: twit.

tweet.ety: Onomatopoeic of the sound made by a bird. Compare twitter. The social media senses evolved from earlier Twitter update, twit (noun), twitter (verb).

ex.en: Did you hear the birds tweeting?
ex.ja: 鳥のさえずり、聞いた？

ex.en: I read your tweet.
ex.ja: ツイート読んだよ。

note.ja: 鳥のさえずりの擬声語。SNS の Twitter での投稿の名前になった。

en: To lie in a position directly beneath something.
To lie under or beneath.

underlie.ety: From Middle English underlien, underliggen, from Old English underliċġan (“to underlie, to be subject to, give way to”), equivalent to under- + lie. Cognate with Dutch onderliggen (“to lie below, lie on the bottom of”), German unterliegen (“to lie under, be subject to, succumb”).

ex.en: The idea underlies his theory.
ex.ja: その考えが彼の理論の基礎となっている。

ex.en: A common theme underlies both perspectives.
ex.ja: 両方の展望にはある共通のテーマがある。

note.ja: under（下に）+ lie（横たわる）。「下に横たわる」→「〜の根底にある」。underlying。

en: Not just.

unfair.ety: From Middle English unfair (“unattractive, unseemly”), from Old English unfæġer (“ugly”), equivalent to un- + fair.

ex.en: You should have refused such an unfair proposal.
ex.ja: そんな不当な提案は、拒否すべきだったのに。

ex.en: The new company rule was unfair to older workers.
ex.ja: 新しい社則は年配の労働者達には不公平だった。

ex.en: She will have it that the conditions are unfair.
ex.ja: 彼女は条件が不公平だと言い張る。

note.ja: un（否定）+ fair（公平な）。「不公平な」。

en: To make an apology or excuse; to acknowledge some fault or offense, with expression of regret for it, by way of amends
To express regret that a certain event has occurred.

apologize.ety: From apology + -ize, from ἀπολογία (apología, “a speech in defense”), from ἀπολογέομαι (apologéomai, “to speak in one’s defense”), from ἀπόλογος (apólogos, “an account, story”), compound of ἀπο- (apo-, “from, off”) and λόγος (lógos, “speech”); compare also ἀπολογίζομαι (apologízomai, “to render an account”).

ex.en: You are to apologize to her for it.
ex.ja: 君はその事について彼女に謝るべきだ。

ex.en: There is no reason for me to apologize.
ex.ja: 私があやまる理由はない。

ex.en: I apologized for having been late for school.
ex.ja: 私は学校に遅れてしまったことを謝った。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 apo（離れて）+ logos（言葉）。自分の非を弁明する言葉（apology）を言う →「謝る」。

en: The solid remains of a fire.
The nonaqueous remains of a material subjected to any complete oxidation process.
To reduce to a residue of ash. See ashing.
To hit the end off (a burning cigar or cigarette).

ex.ja: この火事は全村を灰にしてしまった。

ex.en: The fire reduced the house to ashes.
ex.ja: その火事で家は灰になった。

ex.en: The big fire reduced the whole town to ashes.
ex.ja: 大火事のために町全体が灰になってしまった。

en: The sister or sister-in-law of one’s parent.
The female cousin or cousin-in-law of one’s parent.

ex.en: My aunt speaks Chinese as well as English.
ex.ja: 叔母は英語だけでなく中国語も話します。

ex.en: I went there with my aunt last month.
ex.ja: 叔母といっしょに先月そこへ行った。

note.ja: ラテン語 amita（父方のおば）から古フランス語を経た語。

en: A spherically contained volume of air or other gas in a liquid, commonly a soapy liquid.
A small spherical cavity in a solid material.
To produce bubbles, to rise up in bubbles (such as in foods cooking or liquids boiling).
To churn or foment, as if wishing to rise to the surface.

bubble.ety: Partly imitative, also influenced by burble. Compare Middle Dutch bobbe (“bubble”) > Dutch bubbel (“bubble”), Low German bubbel (“bubble”), Danish boble (“bubble”), Swedish bubbla (“bubble”). The word was first used in its economic sense in association with the collapse of the South Sea Company in 1720, based on the metaphor of an inflated soap bubble bursting.

ex.en: The coffee bubbled in the pot.
ex.ja: コーヒーがポットの中で泡立った。

ex.en: His brain bubbles with new ideas.
ex.ja: 彼の頭は新しいアイディアであふれている。

ex.en: That's because the bubble vanished into thin air.
ex.ja: バブルが跡形もなく消え去ったからである。

note.ja: 中英語 bobel から。擬音的な語。「泡」→ 泡のように膨らんではじける「バブル」。

A person who purchases items for resale in a retail establishment.

ex.ja: 彼らが顧客に売った株は、不良株でした。

en: A public building or room for gambling.
A certain Italian card game for two to four players.

en: The exchange of opinions and advice especially in legal issues; consultation.
Exercise of judgment; prudence.
To give advice, especially professional advice, to (somebody).
To recommend (a course of action).

counsel.ety: From Middle English counseil, conseil, from Old French conseil, from Latin cōnsilium, of unknown origin but possibly from either com- + calō (via a phonetic variant of concilium) or cōnsulō.

ex.en: Recently numerous groups have offered counsel.
ex.ja: 最近多数のグループが助言をしてきた。

ex.en: He makes himself accessible to all who seek his counsel.
ex.ja: 彼は自分の助言を求める人にはみんな面会できるようにしている。

ex.en: Take counsel with a man who is wise and of a good conscience.
ex.ja: 賢明で良心的な人に助言を求めなさい。

note.ja: ラテン語 consilium（相談・助言）から。「助言」→「弁護人」。council（会議）とは別語だが同じく con- から。

en: Causing death; lethal.
Aiming or willing to destroy; implacable; desperately hostile.
In a way which suggests death.
Extremely, incredibly.

From Middle English dedly, dedlych, dedlich, from Old English dēadlīċ (adjective), from Proto-West Germanic *dauþalīk, from Proto-Germanic *dauþalīkaz (“deadly”, literally “deathly”). By surface analysis, dead + -ly. Cognate with Saterland Frisian dodelk (“deadly”), West Frisian deadli

ex.en: He fell a victim to a deadly disease.
ex.ja: 彼は恐ろしい病気にとりつかれた。

ex.en: The party was perfectly deadly.
ex.ja: そのパーティーはまったく退屈だった。

ex.en: She was deadly tired.
ex.ja: 彼女はひどく疲れていた。

note.ja: dead（死んだ）+ -ly（〜のような）。「死をもたらす」→「致命的な」。

en: The act, process, or result of any accurate measurement, as of length, volume, weight, intensity, etc.
The act of defining a concept or notion by giving its essential constituents.

determination.ety: From Middle English determinacion, determynacioun, from Old French determinacion, from Latin dēterminātiō. Morphologically determine + -ation.

ex.en: He made a determination to be a doctor.
ex.ja: 彼は医者になる決心をした。

ex.en: No matter what happens, my determination won't change.
ex.ja: 何事があろうと私は決心を変えない。

ex.en: He was quite decided in his determination.
ex.ja: 彼の決心は確固たるものだった。

note.ja: de（完全に）+ termin（境界）+ ation。境界をはっきり定めること →「決心・決定」。

en: To clasp (someone or each other) in the arms with affection; to take in the arms; to hug.
To seize (something) eagerly or with alacrity; to accept or take up with cordiality; to welcome.
An act of putting arms around someone and bringing the person close to the chest; a hug.
An enclosure partially or fully surrounding someone or something.

embrace.ety: The verb is derived from Middle English embracen (“to clasp in one's arms, embrace; to reach out eagerly for, welcome; to enfold, entwine; to ensnare, entangle; to twist, wrap around; to gird, put on; to lace; to be in or put into bonds; to put a shield on the arm; to grasp (a shield or spear); to acquire, take hold of; to receive; to undertake; to affect, influence; to incite; to unlawfully influence a jury; to surround; to conceal, cover; to shelter; to protect; to comfort; to comprehend, understand”) [and other forms], from Old French embracer, embracier (“to kiss”) (modern French embrasser

ex.en: Shall I stay like this until morning embracing you?
ex.ja: このまま朝までオマエを抱き寄せて過ごそうか。

ex.en: The little boy embraced his dog.
ex.ja: 幼い少年は彼の犬を抱きしめた。

ex.en: They embraced each other.
ex.ja: 彼らは互いに抱きしめ合いました。

note.ja: 古フランス語 embracer ＝ en + brace（両腕）。ラテン語 bracchia。「腕の中に入れる」→「抱きしめる・受け入れる」。bracelet と同じ。

en: To display or show (something) for others to see, especially at an exhibition or contest.
To demonstrate.
An instance of exhibiting.
That which is exhibited.

exhibit.ety: From Latin exhibitus, perfect passive participle of exhibeō (“to hold forth, present, show, display”), from ex (“out of, from”) + habeō (“to have, hold”); see habit.

ex.en: There are some interesting exhibits in the museum.
ex.ja: 博物館には興味深い展示品が所蔵されている。

ex.en: Can I see the special exhibit with this ticket?
ex.ja: この切符で特別展をみられますか。

ex.en: He destroyed the exhibits at the museum.
ex.ja: 彼は美術館の展示物を壊しました。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ hib（持つ）+ it。外に持ち出して見せる →「展示する・示す」。

en: Any well-bred, well-mannered, or charming man.
Any man.

gentleman.ety: From Middle English gentilman, morphologically gentle + man, partial calque of Old French gentilhome.

ex.en: I met a certain gentleman at the station.
ex.ja: 駅である紳士に会った。

ex.en: Ladies and gentlemen, now we start the movie.
ex.ja: みなさま、ただ今より映画を上映いたします。

ex.en: A gentleman is a man of independent means.
ex.ja: ジェントルマンとは独立した財産のある人のことだ。

note.ja: gentle（家柄のよい）+ man。古フランス語 gentilz hom の翻訳。gentle はラテン語 gentilis（同じ一族の）。

en: A tool with a heavy head and a handle used for pounding.
The act of using a hammer to hit something.
To strike repeatedly with a hammer, some other implement, the fist, etc.
To form or forge with a hammer; to shape by beating.

hammer.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Germanic *hamaraz
Proto-West Germanic *hamar
Old English hamor
Middle English hamer
English hammer
From Middle English hamer, from Old English hamor, from Proto-West Germanic *hamar, from Proto-Germanic *hamaraz (“tool with a stone head”) (compare West Frisian hammer, Low German Hamer, Dutch hamer, German Hammer, Danish hammer, Swedish hammare). This is traditionally ascribed to Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱmoros, from *h₂éḱmō (“stone”), but see *hamaraz for further discussion.
(declare a defaulter on the stock exchange): Originally signalled by knocking with a wooden mallet.

ex.en: I took such a hammering over recent months.
ex.ja: この何ヶ月かはひどい打撃を受けました。

ex.en: A hammer was used to break the window.
ex.ja: 窓を割るためにハンマーが使われた。

ex.en: He broke up the concrete block with a hammer.
ex.ja: 彼はハンマーでコンクリートブロックを粉々にした。

note.ja: 古英語 hamor から。もとは「石」の意味とされる。

en: An image, symbol, picture, portrait, or other representation, usually as an object of religious devotion.
A type of religious painting portraying a saint or scene from Scripture, often done on wooden panels.

icon.ety: From Latin īcōn, from Ancient Greek εἰκών (eikṓn, “likeness, image, portrait”). Eastern Orthodox Church sense is attested from 1833. Computing sense first recorded in 1982.

ex.en: This icon is definitely better than the skeleton one. I'm sure of it.
ex.ja: 骸骨のアイコンより、こっちのアイコンの方が絶対いいって。私が保証する。

ex.en: It's troublesome that Internet Explorer's stop icon looks like a shiitake mushroom.
ex.ja: Internet Explorerの中止ボタンがしいたけに見えて困る。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 eikōn（像）から。「聖像」→ 象徴的な「アイコン」。iconic。

en: To apply, enforce, or establish (something, often regarded as burdensome as a restriction or tax: see verb sense 1.2.2) with authority.
To place or put (something chiefly immaterial, especially something regarded as burdensome as a duty, an encumbrance, a penalty, etc.) on…

impose.ety:
The verb is derived from Late Middle English imposen (“to place, set; to impose (a duty, etc.)”), borrowed from Middle French imposer, and Old French emposer, enposer (“to impose (a duty, tax, etc.)”) (modern French imposer), from im-, em- (variants of en- (prefix meaning ‘in, into’)) + poser (“to place, put”), modelled after:
* Latin impōnere (“to place or set (something) on; (figurative) to impose (a duty, tax, etc.)”), from im- (variant of in- (prefix meaning ‘on, upon’)) + pōnō (“to place, put; etc.”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂pó, *h₂epó (“away; off”) + *tḱey- (“to cultivate;

ex.en: The king imposed heavy taxes on the people.
ex.ja: 王は人民に重税を課した。

ex.en: The king imposed heavy taxes on his people.
ex.ja: 王は国民に重い税を課した。

ex.en: The government imposed a new tax on farmers.
ex.ja: 政府は農民に新税を課した。

note.ja: im（上に）+ pos（置く）+ e。上に置いて負わせる →「課す・押し付ける」。

en: Native to a land, especially before colonization.
In particular, of or relating to a people (or their language or culture) that inhabited a region prior to the arrival of people of other …

indigenous.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin indigenus (“native, born in a country”), from indi- (indu-), an old derivative of in (“in”), gen- the root of gignō (“give birth to”), and English -ous. Compare indigene, Ancient Greek ἐνδογενής (endogenḗs, “born in the house”), and the separately formed piecewise doublet endogenous. Unrelated to Indian.

note.ja: ラテン語 indigena（その土地生まれの）から。indu（中に）+ gignere（生む）。「先住の」。gene と同系。

en: Indefinably large, countlessly great; immense.
Boundless, endless, without end or limits; innumerable.
Infinitely many.
Something that is infinite in nature.
A combo that can be used repeatedly without interruption.

infinite.ety: From Middle English infinite, from Old French infinit and its etymon Latin īnfīnītus, from in- (“not”) + fīnis (“end”) + the perfect passive participle ending -ītus. By surface analysis, in- + finite. Doublet of infinito. Displaced native Old English unġeendodlīċ.

ex.en: Are we humans alone in this infinite universe?
ex.ja: この果てしない宇宙にいるのは、私たち人類だけですか？

ex.en: There's no doubt that the universe is infinite.
ex.ja: 宇宙が無限であるということに疑いの余地はない。

ex.en: Evil is easy, and has infinite forms.
ex.ja: 悪は行うに易しくて、その形体も無限である。

note.ja: in（否定）+ finitus（限られた）。「限りのない」。finish、define と同じ fin。

ja: （美術の）インスタレーション

en: An act of installing.
Something installed, especially the whole of a system of machines, apparatus, and accessories, when set up and arranged for practical wor…

installation.ety: From Middle French installation, from Medieval Latin installātiō. By surface analysis, install + -ation. Compare with Piedmontese istallassion.

ex.en: A reboot is required to complete the installation.
ex.ja: インストールを完了するには再起動が必要です。

ex.en: The installation is complete.
ex.ja: インストールが完了しました。

note.ja: install（設置する）+ -ation。「設置・設備」。

en: Of or relating to Iran, its people or its culture.
Pertaining to the Iranian languages or their speakers.
A person from Iran.
A member of any of the various ethnic groups that speak the Iranian languages.

en: A governmental body with the power to make, amend and repeal laws.
The legislative assembly of a province or territory, as opposed to the federal parliament.

legislature.ety: 1676, from stem of legislator + -ure, cognate with French législature.

ex.en: The bill was eviscerated before being passed by the legislature.
ex.ja: 議会を通過しないうちにその法案は骨抜きにされた。

note.ja: legislate（立法する）+ -ure。「立法府」。

en: An obligation, debt or responsibility owed to someone.
Any kind of debt recorded on the right-hand side of a balance sheet.

From liable + -ity.

ex.en: Our company is a limited-liability company.
ex.ja: 我々の会社は有限会社だ。

ex.en: His plan has both virtues and liabilities.
ex.ja: 彼の計画には長所も欠点もある。

ex.en: My unpaid liabilities are still $100.
ex.ja: 私にはまだ未払いの借金が１００ドルある。

note.ja: liable（責任がある）+ -ity。ラテン語 ligare（結ぶ）。「結びつけられていること」→「責任・負債」。

en: A 42.195-kilometre (26-mile-385-yard) road race.
Any extended or sustained activity.
To run a marathon.
To watch or read a large number of instalments of (a film, book, TV series, etc.) in one sitting.

marathon.ety:
