From French marathon, coined in 1894 by linguist Michel Bréal for the first modern time Olympic Games after Ancient Greek Μαραθών (Marathṓn), a town northeast of Athens. Phidippides the Greek ran the distance from Marathon to Athens to deliver a message regarding the Battle of Marathon. The modern sport of marathon running is based on a run approximately the same distance. The toponym itself comes from μάραθον (márathon, “fennel”) an

ex.en: Lots of people took part in the marathon.
ex.ja: たくさんの人々がそのマラソンに参加した。

ex.en: Nobody fell behind in the marathon race.
ex.ja: マラソンで誰も遅れをとらなかった。

ex.en: We will take part in the marathon.
ex.ja: 私たちはそのマラソンに参加するつもりだ。

note.ja: ギリシャの地名マラトン（Marathon）から。戦いの勝利をアテネまで走って伝えた伝説から。

en: That which causes wonder; a prodigy; a portent.
To become filled with wonderment or admiration; to be amazed at something.

marvel.ety: First attested from 1300, from Middle English merveile, from Old French merveille (“a wonder”), from Vulgar Latin *miribilia, from Latin mīrābilia (“wonderful things”), from neuter plural of mīrābilis (“strange, wonderful”), from mīror (“to wonder at”), from mīrus (“wonderful”). Doublet of mirabilia.

ex.en: I marvel how you could agree to the proposal.
ex.ja: 君がなぜ提案に賛成なのか不思議だ。

ex.en: It is a marvel that he should say so.
ex.ja: 彼がそう言うなんて不思議だ。

ex.en: The marvel is that he knew it.
ex.ja: 不思議なのは彼がそれを知っていたことだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 mirabilia（驚くべきもの）から古フランス語を経た語。mirari（驚く）。miracle、admire と同じ mir。

en: In addition to what has been said.

moreover.ety: Inherited from Middle English moreover, moreovere, morover, mooreover, more-overe, mare over, equivalent to more + over.

ex.en: His house is small and moreover it's old.
ex.ja: 彼の住居は小さくてそれに古い。

ex.en: Moreover, how much did you pay for that?
ex.ja: それにいくら払ったの？

ex.en: The house looked good; moreover, the price was right.
ex.ja: 家はかなりにみえたし、しかも値段が手頃だった。

note.ja: more（さらに）+ over（その上に）。「そのうえ」。

en: Synonym of military parade: A show of troops, an assembly of troops as a show of force, to receive orders, or especially for inspection a…
A public procession, especially one commemorating a holiday or special event or (dated) in protest.
To assemble for inspection, to receive orders, etc.
To march impressively or ostentatiously.

parade.ety: From French parade (“an ostentatious display, a military display”), from parer (“to beautify, prepare, take pride in”) + -ade probably under influence from earlier Italian parata (“preparation, a military parade, an ostentatious display”) and Latin magnō parātū (“with great preparation”). Various senses similarly influenced by earlier French and Italian uses. Doublet of pare.

ex.en: A band led the parade through the city.
ex.ja: 楽隊が先頭に立って市を行進した。

ex.en: It was a parade with a capital P.
ex.ja: それはこの上なくすばらしいパレードだった。

ex.en: The parade was led by an army band.
ex.ja: そのパレードは軍楽隊に先導された。

note.ja: フランス語 parade から。スペイン語 parada（止まること）、ラテン語 parare（準備する）。閲兵の整列 →「行進」。prepare と同じ。

en: The place where sanctified souls are believed to live after death.
A very pleasant place, such as a place full of lush vegetation.
To place (as) in paradise.

paradise.ety: From Middle English paradis, paradise, paradys, from Late Old English paradīs, borrowed from Old French paradis, from Latin paradīsus, from Ancient Greek παράδεισος (parádeisos), ultimately from Proto-Iranian *paridayjah. Doublet of parvis. Displaced Old English neorxnawang.

ex.en: The island is a paradise for children.
ex.ja: その島は子供にとっては楽園です。

ex.en: This park is a paradise for children.
ex.ja: この公園は子供の楽園だ。

ex.en: This beach is a paradise for surfers.
ex.ja: このビーチはサーファーにはパラダイスだ。

note.ja: ペルシャ語 pairidaēza（囲われた庭）からギリシャ語を経た語。「庭園」→「楽園」。

en: To become aware of, through the physical senses, to see; to understand.
To interpret something in a particular way.

perceive.ety: From Middle English perceyven, borrowed from Old French percevoir, perceveir, from Latin percipiō, past participle perceptus (“take hold of, obtain, receive, observe”), from per (“by, through”) + capiō (“to take”); see capable. Compare conceive, deceive, receive.

ex.en: I perceive by your face that you have good news.
ex.ja: あなたの表情から良い知らせがあるとすぐ分かります。

ex.en: Nobody perceived me entering the room.
ex.ja: 誰も私が部屋に入って来たことに気づかなかった。

ex.en: He could not perceive any difference between the twins.
ex.ja: 彼はその双子の違いを何ら気づく事が出来なかった。

note.ja: per（完全に）+ ceiv（つかむ）+ e。しっかりつかみ取る →「知覚する・気づく」。

en: In preparation for the main matter; initial, introductory, preparatory.
A preparation for a main matter; an introduction.
Any of a series of sports events that determine the finalists.

preliminary.ety: Borrowed from New Latin praelīmināris, formed from prae- (“before”) + līmen (“threshold”) + -āris (adjectival suffix); compare Latin līmināris (“of or belonging to a threshold”). Compare French préliminaire.

ex.en: Regretfully, the Japanese representative was eliminated at the preliminary stage.
ex.ja: 日本代表は惜しくも予選敗退となりました。

note.ja: pre（前の）+ limen（敷居）+ -ary。「敷居をまたぐ前の」→「予備の」。eliminate と同じ limin。

en: The first showing of a film, play or other form of entertainment, often held as a special event with celebrity guests.
The first episode of a television show or a particular season of that show.
Of a film or play, to play for the first time.
To present a film or play for the first time.

ex.en: I guarantee a huge audience for tonight's premiere.
ex.ja: 今夜の初日はきっと大にぎわいになりますよ。

note.ja: フランス語 première（最初の）から。ラテン語 primarius。「初演」。prime と同じ。

en: The office or role of president.
The bureaucratic organization and governmental initiatives devolving directly from the president.

presidency.ety: From Medieval Latin praesidentia. By surface analysis, president + -cy.

ex.en: He is going to run for the Presidency.
ex.ja: 彼は大統領に立候補するだろう。

ex.en: He made a hard run of the presidency.
ex.ja: 彼は大統領選挙で懸命に戦った。

ex.en: He is a natural to win the Presidency.
ex.ja: 彼は必ず大統領の椅子につく人物だ。

note.ja: president（大統領）+ -cy。「大統領職」。

en: To act in response.
To return an impulse or impression; to resist the action of another body by an opposite force

ex.en: C is formed by reacting A with B.
ex.ja: AとBを反応させるとCが生成されます。

ex.en: How did he react to the bad news?
ex.ja: 彼はその悪い知らせにどんな反応を示しましたか。

ex.en: The audience reacted in different ways to her performance.
ex.ja: 観客は彼女の演奏にさまざまな反応を示した。

note.ja: re（逆に）+ act（作用する）。「反応する」。

en: Expressed or represented as being accurate, practicable, or not idealistic.
Relating to the representation of objects, actions or conditions as they actually are or were.

ex.en: The long discussion reached a realistic conclusion.
ex.ja: 長い議論は現実的な結論に煮詰まった。

ex.en: Are today's video game images this realistic?
ex.ja: 今のゲームの映像はここまでリアルになってんのか？

ex.en: I hope my boss will agree to my realistic plan.
ex.ja: 上司が私の現実的な計画に賛成してくれることを希望する。

note.ja: realist + -ic。real（現実の）。「現実的な」。

en: An act of pointing out or noticing; notice or observation.
An expression, in speech or writing, of something remarked or noticed; a mention of something
To pay heed to; notice; to take notice of, to perceive.
To express in words or writing; to state, as an observation.

remark.ety: From Middle French remarquer, from Old French remarquer, from re- (“again”) + marquer (“to mark”), equivalent to re- (“again”) + mark.

ex.en: That was not at all an appropriate remark.
ex.ja: あれはどうも適切な発言ではなかった。

ex.en: I remarked on the beauty of the landscape.
ex.ja: 私は、風景の美しさについて、述べた。

ex.en: She may well be angry at his remark.
ex.ja: 彼のことばに彼女が腹を立てているのも無理はない。

note.ja: フランス語 remarquer ＝ re + marquer（印をつける）。「気づく」→「述べる・発言」。remarkable と同じ。

en: Often followed by from: to hold back (someone or something); to check, to prevent, to restrain, to stop.
To hold back (a pupil) instead of allowing them to advance to the next class or year; to keep back.

retain.ety: From Late Middle English reteinen, retein (“to continue to keep, retain; to continue to possess; to possess; to contain; to draw back, retire; to hold back, restrain; to keep in mind, remember; to take back, repossess; to appoint; to engage in one’s service, employ, hire”) [and other forms], from Anglo-Norman reteiner, retenir [and other forms], Middle French retenir, and Old French retenir (“to keep back, retain; to keep, maintain, preserve; to possess; to engage in one’s service, employ; to detain; to hold back, restrain; to remember”) (modern French retenir), from Vulgar Latin *retinīre, fr

ex.en: If you use a computer, you can retain information.
ex.ja: コンピューターを使えば情報を保持することができる。

ex.en: This town still retains something of the old days.
ex.ja: この町はいまだに昔の面影をとどめている。

ex.en: I'd retain that old hat if I were you.
ex.ja: 私があなただったら、その古い帽子を取っておくだろうに。

note.ja: re（後ろに）+ tain（保つ）。後ろに保っておく →「保持する・維持する」。

en: A fulfilment of a need or desire.
The pleasure obtained by the fulfillment of one or more needs or desires; a sense of contentment with one's situation and achievements.

satisfaction.ety: From Middle English satisfaccioun, from Old French satisfaccion and Latin satisfactiō, satisfactiōnis.

ex.en: We hope this will be to your satisfaction.
ex.ja: これはきっと気に入って頂けると思います。

ex.en: His success was a great satisfaction to me.
ex.ja: 彼の成功は私にとって大きな喜びでした。

ex.en: It would be a satisfaction to me.
ex.ja: そうしてもらったら私は満足だ。

note.ja: sat（十分に）+ is + fact（する）+ ion。十分にすること →「満足」。satisfy（満足させる）。

en: To rub a surface with a sharp object, especially by a living creature to remove itching with nails, claws, etc.
To rub the skin with rough material causing a sensation of irritation; to cause itching.
A disruption, mark or shallow cut on a surface made by scratching.
An act of scratching the skin to alleviate an itch or irritation.
For or consisting of preliminary or tentative, incomplete, etc. work.
Hastily assembled, arranged or constructed, from whatever materials are to hand, with little or no preparation

scratch.ety:
From Middle English scracchen, of uncertain origin. Potentially a blend of Middle English scratten (“to scratch”) and cracchen (“to scratch”). Ultimately onomatopoeic. More at scrat and cratch.
Compare Old English scrama, Old Norse skråma, German Schramme (“scratch”), which may be related.

ex.en: I can hear a cat scratching at the window.
ex.ja: 猫が窓を引っかいているのが聞こえる。

ex.en: I'm not going to buy that CD. It's scratched.
ex.ja: そんなCD買うつもりなんてないよ。傷だらけじゃないか。

ex.en: The cat is scratching at my door.
ex.ja: 猫がドアをカリカリしてるわ。

note.ja: 中英語 scratten から。擬音的な語。「ひっかく」→ 競技のスタートラインを地面にひっかいて引いたことから from scratch（ゼロから）。

en: Darkness where light, particularly sunlight, is blocked.
Something that blocks light, particularly in a window.
To shield (someone or something) from light.
To alter slightly.

shade.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *(s)ḱeh₃-
Proto-Indo-European *(s)ḱh₃tús
Proto-Germanic *skaduz
Proto-West Germanic *skadu
Old English sċeadu
Middle English schade
English shade
Inherited from Middle English schade, from Old English sċeadu, from Proto-West Germanic *skadu, from Proto-Germanic *skaduz, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ḱh₃tús, from *(s)ḱeh₃-. Doublet of shadow. Cognate with Ancient Greek σκότος (skótos) (whence English scoto-) and σκιά (skiá) (whence English scia-, and uncertainly via σκίουρος (skíouros) English squirrel).

ex.en: Mary stood with her hand shading her eyes.
ex.ja: メアリーは手を目にかざして立っていた。

ex.en: Paul stood with his hand shading his eyes.
ex.ja: ポールは目を手で覆いながら立っていた。

ex.en: They sat in the shade of a tree.
ex.ja: 彼らは木蔭に座った。

note.ja: 古英語 sceadu から。shadow と同じ語。「日陰」→「色合い・ニュアンス」→（shades）サングラス。

en: (High Sheriff) An official of a shire or county office, responsible for carrying out court orders, law enforcement and other duties.
A judge in the sheriff court, the court of a county or sheriffdom.
To carry out the duties of a sheriff.

sheriff.ety: Inherited from Middle English shirreve, in turn inherited from Old English sċīrġerēfa, corresponding to shire + reeve. There is no etymological connection to sharif (Arabic شَرِيف (šarīf)), an Arabic title of honour with cognates in other languages, including Persian, Punjabi, Bengali, Hindi, Urdu, Turkish, Spanish, Portuguese, etc.

ex.en: The sheriff established order in the town.
ex.ja: 保安官は、その町の秩序を確立した。

ex.en: The sheriff beat the suspect until he was almost dead.
ex.ja: 保安官は容疑者を相手が死んでしまうのではないかと思われるまで何回も殴りつけた。

note.ja: 古英語 scīrgerēfa ＝ shire（州）+ reeve（役人）。「州の役人」→「保安官」。

en: Easily frightened; timid.
Reserved; disinclined to familiar approach.
To avoid due to caution, embarrassment or timidness.
To jump back in fear.
An act of throwing.
A place for throwing.

shy.ety: From Middle English shy (“shy”), from Old English sċēoh (“shy”), from Proto-West Germanic *skeuh (“shy, fearful”), from Proto-Germanic *skeuhaz (“shy, fearful”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian skjou (“shy”), Dutch schuw (“shy”), German scheu (“shy”), Danish sky (“shy”).

ex.en: She seems the least shy of the three.
ex.ja: その３人の中では、彼女が一番内気ではなさそうだ。

ex.en: The fact is that my cat is shy.
ex.ja: 実はわたしの猫は恥ずかしがり屋なのです。

ex.en: She used to be a very shy girl.
ex.ja: 昔はとても内気な女の子だったからね。

note.ja: 古英語 scēoh（臆病な）から。「おびえやすい」→「内気な」。

en: At an indefinite but stated time in the past or future.
Former, erstwhile; at some previous time.
Occasional; intermittent.

sometime.ety: From Middle English somtyme, som time, some tyme, sume time, sumtym, sumtyme, equivalent to some + time.

ex.en: I hope we'll see each other again sometime.
ex.ja: またお会いできるといいですね。

ex.en: I would like to see you again sometime.
ex.ja: またいつかお会いしたいものです。

ex.en: We must get together for a drink sometime.
ex.ja: いつか集まって一杯やらなくてはいけないね。

note.ja: some + time。「いつか」。sometimes（ときどき）と区別。

en: In a strict manner.
In a limited manner; only.

strictly.ety:
Etymology tree
English strict
Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der.
Proto-Germanic *līkąder.

Proto-West Germanic *-līkē

English strictly
From strict + -ly.

ex.en: Speaking strictly, your opinion is different from mine.
ex.ja: 厳密に言えば、あなたと私の意見は違う。

ex.en: Strictly speaking, they are not the same variety.
ex.ja: 厳密に言えば、それらは同じ種類ではない。

ex.en: Strictly speaking, she's not qualified for the job.
ex.ja: 厳密に言えば、彼女はその仕事をする資格がないと言う事です。

note.ja: strict（厳しい）+ -ly。ラテン語 stringere（締めつける）。「厳密に」。

en: The direct rays, light or warmth of the sun.
A location on which the sun's rays fall.
Open to and permitting public access, especially with regard to activities that were previously closed-door or back-room meetings.

sunshine.ety: In the Coverdale Bible in 1535, in Genesis and Exodus about 1250 as Middle English sunnesine; synchronically sun + shine. Compare isolated Old English sunsċīn (“mirror”).

ex.en: This room gets a lot of sunshine.
ex.ja: この部屋は良く日が当たる。

ex.en: The children were playing in the sunshine.
ex.ja: 子供達は日なたで遊んでいた。

ex.en: You can get energy from the sunshine.
ex.ja: 日光からエネルギーを得る事ができる。

note.ja: sun（太陽）+ shine（輝き）。「日光」。

en: One who ties (knots, etc.).
Something that ties.
To arrange in layers.
To cascade in an overlapping sequence.

ex.en: Tom is a graduate of a top-tier university.
ex.ja: トムは一流大学出身です。

note.ja: 古フランス語 tire（列・順序）から。「段・層」。※ tie（結ぶ）+ -er とは別語源。

en: Of, pertaining to, or resembling the human voice or speech.
Used in the production of speech sounds.
A vocal sound; specifically, a purely vocal element of speech, unmodified except by resonance; a vowel or a diphthong; a tonic element; a…
A part of a piece of music that is sung.

vocal.ety:

Late Middle English vocal, borrowed from Latin vōcālis (“uttering a voice, sounding, speaking”), from vōx (“a voice, sound, tone”) + -ālis (“-al”, adjectival suffix). Doublet of vowel and vocalis. Compare Old French vocal.

ex.en: Public feeling against air pollution has at last become vocal.
ex.ja: 大気汚染に対しての世論がついにやかましくなった。

ex.en: Do fish have vocal cords?
ex.ja: 魚に声帯はありますか？

note.ja: voc（声）+ al。声の →「声の・声高に主張する・ボーカル」。

en: To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.
To produce as return from an investment.
A product.
Measurement of the amount of a crop harvested, or animal products such as wool, meat or milk produced, per unit area of land.

yield.ety:
From Middle English yielden, yelden, ȝelden (“to yield, pay”), from Old English ġieldan (“to pay”), from Proto-West Germanic *geldan (“to pay”), from Proto-Germanic *geldaną (“to pay”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰeldʰ- (“to pay”). Doublet of geld.
The noun is from Middle English ȝeld (“tax, payment”), from Old English ġield (“payment”), from Proto-West Germanic *geld (“payment”), from Proto-Germanic *geldą (“reward, gift, money”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰeldʰ- (“to pay”).
Cognates
Cognate with Scots yield (“to yield”), North Frisian jilden (“to pay”), Saterland Frisian jäilde (“to be vali

ex.en: He yields to nobody in love of music.
ex.ja: 音楽が好きなことでは彼は誰にも負けない。

ex.en: Our land gave a high yield this year.
ex.ja: 今年はずいぶん収穫があった。

ex.en: I did not yield to such a rule.
ex.ja: 私はそのような規則に従わなかった。

note.ja: 古英語 gieldan（支払う）から。「支払う」→「生み出す・もたらす」→ 譲る・「屈する」。

en: To finish successfully.
To complete, as time or distance.

accomplish.ety:
From Middle English accomplisshen, acomplissen, from Old French acompliss-, extended stem of acomplir (Modern French accomplir), from Vulgar Latin *(ac)complīre, from Latin complēre (“fill up/out, complete”, whence English complete).
First attested in the late 14th century.

ex.en: This task is impossible for me to accomplish.
ex.ja: その仕事は私には無理だよ。

ex.en: The task will be accomplished in a year.
ex.ja: その仕事は１年で完成するでしょう。

ex.en: We could accomplish what we had started before.
ex.ja: 私たちは以前始めたことを成し遂げることができた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 acomplir（成し遂げる）から。ad + complere（満たす）。「完全に満たす」→「成し遂げる」。complete と同じ。

en: The act or practice of admitting.
Permission to enter, or the entrance itself; admittance; entrance; access

admission.ety: Borrowed from Latin admissio, admissionis; compare French admission. See admit.

ex.en: Admission to the show is by ticket only.
ex.ja: 芝居にはきっぷを持っている人だけ入れます。

ex.en: He applied for admission to the riding club.
ex.ja: 彼はその乗馬クラブへ入会を申しこんだ。

ex.en: The admission is ten dollars a person.
ex.ja: 入場料は一人10ドルです。

note.ja: ad（〜へ）+ miss（送る）+ ion。中へ送り入れること →「入場（料）・入学・告白（認めること）」。

en: Cured meat from the sides, belly, or back of a pig.
Such meat from the belly specifically.

bacon.ety:
From Middle English bacoun (“meat from the back and sides of a pig”), from Anglo-Norman bacon, bacun (“ham, flitch, strip of lard”), from Old Low Frankish *bakō (“ham, flitch”), from Proto-Germanic *bakô, *bakkô (“back”), an extension of *baką, whence English back, which see for more. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeg- (“back, buttocks; to vault, arch”).
Cognate with Old Saxon baco (“back”), Dutch bake (“ham, side of bacon”), Old High German bahho (“ham, side of bacon”), whence German Bache f (“wild sow”), Alemannic German Bache m (“bacon”).
(police): Extension of pig (“police”).

ex.en: Bacon and eggs is his order.
ex.ja: ベーコンエッグは彼が注文したものだ。

ex.en: Don't eat bacon at night because it has a lot of fat.
ex.ja: ベーコンは脂肪分が多いから、夜は食べちゃダメよ。

ex.en: Would you like bacon or sausage?
ex.ja: ベーコンかソーセージはいかがか。

note.ja: 古フランス語 bacon（豚の背肉）から。ゲルマン語 bakkon（背中）。back と同系。

en: A structure that bars passage.
An obstacle or impediment.
To block or obstruct with a barrier.

barrier.ety: From Middle English barrer, barrere, barryȝer, from Anglo-Norman barrere (compare French barrière), from barre (“bar”).

ex.en: We must work hard to break down social barriers.
ex.ja: 我々は社会的障壁を取り壊すために、懸命に努力しなければならない。

ex.en: Show your ticket at the barrier.
ex.ja: 改札口で切符をお見せください。

ex.en: Trade barriers were lifted after the war ended.
ex.ja: 貿易障壁は戦争終結後解除されました。

note.ja: 古フランス語 barriere から。barre（棒）。「棒の柵」→「障壁」。bar と同じ。

en: To break from internal pressure.
To cause to break from internal pressure.
An act or instance of bursting.
A sudden, often intense, expression, manifestation or display.

burst.ety:
From Middle English bresten, bersten, from Old English berstan, from Proto-West Germanic *brestan, from Proto-Germanic *brestaną, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰres- (“to burst, break, crack, split, separate”), enlargement of *bʰreHi- (“to snip, split”).
See also West Frisian boarste, Dutch barsten, Danish briste, Swedish brista; also Irish bris (“to break”)). More at brine. Also cognate to debris.

ex.en: On hearing the joke, he burst out laughing.
ex.ja: その冗談を聞いて彼は突然笑い出した。

ex.en: They burst out into a storm of abuse.
ex.ja: 彼らは激しくののしり始めた。

ex.en: She burst into tears upon hearing the news.
ex.ja: 彼女はその知らせを聞いて突然泣き出した。

note.ja: 古英語 berstan から。「破裂する」→「突然〜しだす」（burst into tears）。

en: Domesticated animals of the species Bos taurus (cows, bulls, steers, oxen etc), and other hoofed mammals of the genus Bos.
Certain other livestock, such as sheep, pigs or goats. Also rarely applied to horses.

cattle.ety:
From Middle English catel, from Anglo-Norman catel (“personal property”), from Old Northern French (compare French cheptel, Old French chetel, chatel, also English chattel) from Medieval Latin capitāle, from Latin capitālis (“of the head”) (whence also capital, from caput (“head”) + -alis (“-al”)). For the sense evolution, compare pecuniary and fee. Also compare Russian поголо́вье (pogolóvʹje, “total number of livestock”) from Russian голова́ (golová, “head”). Doublet of capital and chattel.
Compare Old Dutch katēl ("moveable property, head of cattle"; whence Middle Dutch cateele, cateile, cat

ex.en: He learned how to raise cattle.
ex.ja: 彼は牛の飼育の仕方を知った。

ex.en: We have ten head of cattle.
ex.ja: うちには十頭の牛がいる。

ex.en: Their cattle are all fat.
ex.ja: 家畜はみんなまるまるしている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 chatel（財産）から。ラテン語 capitale（主要な財産）。家畜が主要な財産だったことから。capital、chattel と同じ語源。

en: A room, often in a school, where classes take place.

classroom.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *kelh₁-der.
Proto-Italic *klāssis
Latin classisder.
Middle French classebor.
English class
Proto-Indo-European *Hrew-?
Proto-Indo-European *(H)rewH-der.
Proto-Germanic *rūmą
Proto-West Germanic *rūm
Old English rūm
Middle English roum
English room
English classroom
From class + room.

ex.en: There is a tall man in the classroom.
ex.ja: 教室に背の高い男の人が一人います。

ex.en: There were few students left in the classroom.
ex.ja: 教室には生徒はほとんど残っていなかった。

ex.en: There were few students remaining in the classroom.
ex.ja: 教室にはほとんど学生は残っていませんでした。

note.ja: class（授業）+ room。「教室」。

en: The settlement of differences by arbitration or by consent reached by mutual concessions.
A committal to something derogatory or objectionable; a prejudicial concession; a surrender.
To bind by mutual agreement.
To adjust and settle by mutual concessions; to compound.

compromise.ety: From Middle French compromis, from Medieval Latin, Late Latin compromissum (“a compromise, originally a mutual promise to refer to arbitration”), prop. neuter of Latin compromissus, past participle of compromittere (“to make a mutual promise to abide by the decision of an arbiter”), from com- (“together”) + promittere (“to promise”); see promise.

ex.en: The mayor will compromise to a certain extent.
ex.ja: 市長はある程度妥協するだろう。

ex.en: Both sides had to compromise with each other.
ex.ja: 双方が互いに歩み寄らねばならなかった。

ex.en: There seems to be no possibility of compromise.
ex.ja: 妥協の可能性はないように思える。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pro（前に）+ mis（送る）+ e。互いに約束を差し出すこと →「妥協（する）・危うくする」。

en: Serving to reduce a difficulty, or accessible with minimum difficulty; expedient.
Suspicious due to suiting someone's purposes very well.

convenient.ety: From Middle English convenient, from Latin conveniēns (“fit, suitable, convenient”), present participle of conveniō, convinīre (“to come together, suit”); see convene and compare covenant.

ex.en: It's convenient living so close to the station.
ex.ja: こんなに駅に近くに住んでいると便利ですよ。

ex.en: These convenient goods will meet our customers' demands.
ex.ja: これらの便利な商品は私達のお客様の需要を満たすだろう。

ex.en: We feel that March 1 would be more convenient.
ex.ja: ３月１日の方が都合がよいのですが。

note.ja: con（共に）+ veni（来る）+ ent。うまく一緒にやって来る →「都合のよい・便利な」。

en: A plant, grown for it, or its fruits or seeds, to be harvested as food, livestock fodder, or fuel or for any other economic purpose.
The production amount of such an output for a specific season or year, particularly of plants.
To remove the top end of something, especially a plant.
To mow, reap or gather.

crop.ety:
From Middle English crop, croppe, from Old English cropp, croppa (“the head or top of a plant, a sprout or herb, a bunch or cluster of flowers, an ear of corn, the craw of a bird, a kidney”), from Proto-West Germanic *kropp, from Proto-Germanic *kruppaz (“body, trunk, crop”), from Proto-Indo-European *grewb- (“to warp, bend, crawl”). In Euclidean spaces: a set of points obtained by adding a given fixed vector to each point of a given set.

translate.ety:
From Middle English translaten (“to transport, translate, transform”), from Anglo-Norman translater, from Latin trānslātus, perfect passive participle of trānsferō (“to transport, carry across, translate”). See also -ate (verb-forming suffix). Distant doublet of transfer, see collate and confer, delate and defer, as well as prelate and prefer among others.
In this sense, displaced Old English wendan (“to translate,” also the word for “to turn” and “to change”).

ex.en: Don't translate English into Japanese word for word.
ex.ja: 英語を逐語的に日本語訳してはいけない。

ex.en: The novel has been translated into many languages.
ex.ja: その小説は多くの言語に翻訳されてきた。

ex.en: We translated the novel from Japanese into English.
ex.ja: 私たちはその小説を日本語から英語に訳した。

note.ja: trans（向こうへ）+ lat（運ばれた）+ e。向こう側へ運ぶ →「翻訳する・置き換える」。

en: Requiring immediate attention.
Of people: insistent, solicitous.

urgent.ety: Borrowed from Middle French urgent (“pressing, impelling”), from Latin urgēns, from urgēre (“to press”), from Proto-Indo-European *werǵʰ- (“bind, squeeze”). Equivalent to urge + -ent. Related to German würgen (“to strangle”), Lithuanian ver̃žti (“to string, tighten, constrict”), Russian (poetic) отверза́ть (otverzátʹ, “to open”, literally “to untie”), Polish otwierać (“to open”)) and English worry, wring, wreak, wreck.

ex.en: I have an urgent matter to attend to.
ex.ja: 急いでする事がある。

ex.en: The question before us is an urgent one.
ex.ja: 我々の直面している問題は緊急のものだ。

ex.en: He had some urgent news to tell me.
ex.ja: 彼には僕に話したい緊急の知らせがあった。

note.ja: ラテン語 urgere（押し迫る）から。「差し迫った」→「緊急の」。urge と同じ。

en: A plant raised for some edible part of it, such as the leaves, roots, fruit or flowers, but excluding any plant considered to be a fruit,…
The edible part of such a plant.
Of or relating to plants.
Of or relating to vegetables.

vegetable.ety:

From Middle English vegetable, from Old French vegetable, from Latin vegetābilis (“able to live and grow”), derived from vegetāre (“to enliven”). Displaced Old English wyrt and ofett, whence modern w

ex.en: What do you call this vegetable in English?
ex.ja: この野菜は英語で何と言いますか。

ex.en: Can I use this area to raise vegetables?
ex.ja: この場所を野菜を作るのに使っていいですか。

ex.en: I bought eggs, meat, vegetables, and what not.
ex.ja: 私は卵や肉や野菜やその他いろいろの物を買った。

note.ja: ラテン語 vegetabilis（成長させる）から。vegere（活気づける）。「生長するもの」→「野菜」。vigor と同系。

en: Standing, pointing, or moving straight up or down; parallel to the local direction of gravity; along the direction of a plumb line; perpe…
In a two-dimensional Cartesian co-ordinate system, describing the axis y oriented normal (perpendicular, at right angles) to the horizont…
A vertex or zenith.
A vertical geometrical figure; a perpendicular.

vertical.ety: Borrowed from Middle French vertical, from Late Latin verticālis.

ex.en: He drew some vertical lines on the paper.
ex.ja: 彼は紙のうえに垂直な線を何本か引いた。

ex.en: Strictly speaking, it was not a vertical line.
ex.ja: 厳密に言えば、それは垂直線ではなかった。

ex.en: That pole is not quite vertical.
ex.ja: その柱は垂直になっていない。

note.ja: ラテン語 vertex（頂点・回転軸）から。vert（回る）。頂点に向かう →「垂直の・縦の」。

en: An infraction or a failure to follow a rule.
Rape; sexual activity forced on another person without their consent.

violation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French violation, from Latin violātiō (“injury, profanation”), from violō (“to treat with violence; to maltreat; to violate, defile, profane”). Morphologically violate + -ion.

ex.en: I don't agree with violation of human rights.
ex.ja: 私は人権侵害に反対だ。

ex.en: The local police are very strict about traffic violations.
ex.ja: 地元の警察は交通違反にはとても厳しい。

ex.en: I was fined six thousand yen for a parking violation.
ex.ja: 駐車違反で６０００円の罰金をとられた。

note.ja: violate（違反する）+ -ion。ラテン語 violare（暴力をふるう）、vis（力）。violent と同じ。

en: A small case, often flat and often made of leather, for keeping money (especially paper money), credit cards, etc.
A person's bank account or assets.

wallet.ety: From Middle English walet (“a bag, knapsack”), of uncertain origin. Possibly from an assumed Old Northern French *walet (“a roll; bag; a knapsack”), from Proto-Germanic *wal- (“to roll”). More at walk, well, wallow.

ex.en: Did you see a brown wallet around here?
ex.ja: この辺で茶色い財布を見ませんでしたか。

ex.en: There was no money left in my wallet.
ex.ja: 財布にはお金が少しも残っていなかった。

ex.en: I have no more money in my wallet.
ex.ja: 財布に金が無くなった。

note.ja: 中英語 walet（旅の袋）から。語源ははっきりしない。「財布」。

en: A room, especially one which is not particularly large, used for manufacturing or other light industrial work.
A brief, intensive course of education for a small group, emphasizing interaction and practical problem solving.
To help a playwright revise a draft of (a play) by rehearsing it with actors and critiquing the results.
To work on or revise something, especially collaboratively, in a workshop.

ex.en: He's making a table in his workshop.
ex.ja: 彼は仕事場でテーブルを作っているところだ。

ex.en: The basement has been made over into a workshop.
ex.ja: 地下室を仕事場に改造した。

ex.en: Please give us a call now if you want to participate in the workshop.
ex.ja: この講習会に参加をご希望のかたは、今すぐお電話ください。

note.ja: work（仕事）+ shop（作業場）。「作業場」→「研修会」。

en: On board; into or within a ship or boat; hence, into or within a railway car.
On or onto a horse, a camel, etc.
On board of; onto or into a ship, boat, train, plane.
Onto a horse.

aboard.ety: From Middle English abord, from a- (“on”) + bord (“board, side of a ship”); equivalent to a- + board.

ex.en: How many people were aboard that ship?
ex.ja: その船には何人の人が乗ってたんですか？

ex.en: I feel as if I were aboard a great ship.
ex.ja: 大船に乗った気持ちがする。

ex.en: They are now aboard the ship.
ex.ja: 彼らは今船に乗っている。

note.ja: a（〜に）+ board（船べり・甲板）。「船の上に」→「乗って」。

en: An abridgement or summary of a longer publication.
Something that concentrates in itself the qualities of a larger item, or multiple items.
Not concrete: conceptual, ideal.
Insufficiently factual.
To separate; to disengage.
To remove; to take away; withdraw.

abstract.ety: From Middle English abstract, borrowed from Latin abstractus, perfect passive participle of abstrahō (“draw away”), formed from abs- (“away”) + trahō (“to pull, draw”). The verbal sense is first attested in 1542.

ex.en: The theory is too abstract for me.
ex.ja: その理論は私にはちんぷんかんぷんだ。

ex.en: The new theory is too abstract for ordinary people.
ex.ja: その新しい理論は一般人には難しすぎる。

ex.en: Your explanation is too abstract to me.
ex.ja: あなたの説明は私には抽象的すぎます。

note.ja: abs（離れて）+ tract（引く）。具体物から引き離した →「抽象的な・要約」。

en: A higher-pitched or stronger (louder or longer) articulation of a particular syllable of a word or phrase in order to distinguish it from…
Emphasis or importance in general.
To express the accent of vocally; to utter with accent.
To mark emphatically; to emphasize; to accentuate; to make prominent.

accent.ety:

Middle English accent
English accent
Inherited from Middle English accent, from Medieval Latin accentus and Old French accent, acent, both from Latin accentus, past participle of accinō (“sing to, sing along”),

ex.en: The man speaks English with a German accent.
ex.ja: その男はドイツ語なまりの英語を話す。

ex.en: Ask your teacher where to place the accent.
ex.ja: 先生にどこにアクセントを置くかを聞きなさい。

ex.en: His policy puts the accent on national welfare.
ex.ja: 彼の政策は国民の福祉に重点を置く。

note.ja: ラテン語 accentus ＝ ad + cantus（歌）。「言葉に添えた調子」→「アクセント・なまり」。chant と同じ。

en: A state that is characterized by compulsive drug use or compulsive engagement in rewarding behavior, despite negative consequences.
The state of being addicted; devotion; inclination.

addiction.ety: From addict + -ion; compare (Latin) addictio (“an adjudging, an award”).

ex.en: Drug addiction is a cancer in modern society.
ex.ja: 麻薬中毒は現代社会の癌だ。

ex.en: There really is such a thing as Internet addiction.
ex.ja: インターネット中毒って、本当にあるみたいね。

ex.en: Tom has been in clinical treatment for addiction for the last five years.
ex.ja: トムはここ5年、嗜癖の臨床治療を続けています。

note.ja: addict（中毒にする）+ -ion。ラテン語 addicere（引き渡す）、ad + dicere（言う）。「（判決で）引き渡されること」→「依存」。

en: Not asleep; conscious.
Alert, aware.
To become conscious after having slept.
To cause (somebody) to stop sleeping.

From Middle English awake, a shortened form of awaken (“awakened, awake”), past participle of Middle English awaken (“to awaken”). See verb below. Compare Saterland Frisian woak (“awake”), German Low German waak (“awake”), German wach (“awake”).

ex.en: I awoke one morning and found myself famous.
ex.ja: ある朝目覚めたらば、私は有名になっていた。

ex.en: I awoke one morning to find myself famous.
ex.ja: ある朝目がさめたら私は有名になっていた。

ex.en: When I awoke this morning, I felt hungry.
ex.ja: 今朝目が覚めたとき、空腹感を覚えた。

note.ja: a（強意）+ wake（目を覚ます）。「目が覚めて」。

en: Any large piece of timber or iron long in proportion to its thickness, and prepared for use.
One of the principal horizontal structural members, usually of steel, timber, or concrete, of a building.
To emit beams of light; to shine; to radiate.
To smile broadly or especially cheerfully.

Cognate with North Frisian Boom, buum (“tree”), Saterland Frisian Boom (“tree”), West Frisian beam (“tree”), Cimbrian pome, póom, puam (“tree”), Dutch boom (“tree”), German Low German Boom (“tree”), G

ex.en: This program is beamed from US to Japan.
ex.ja: この番組はアメリカから日本へ送られている。

ex.en: We beamed the message to the world.
ex.ja: 我々は世界中にそのメッセージを送った。

ex.en: Beams bear the weight of the roof.
ex.ja: 梁が屋根をささえている。

note.ja: 古英語 bēam（木・梁）から。ドイツ語 Baum（木）と同じ。「梁」→ 梁のようにまっすぐな「光線」。

en: Any plant of several genera of the taxonomic family Fabaceae that produces large edible seeds or edible seedpods.
The large edible seed of such a plant (for example, a broad bean, navy bean, or garbanzo bean).
To hit with a projectile, especially a deliberately aimed blow to the head.

From Middle English bene, from Old English bēan, from Proto-West Germanic *baunu, from Proto-Germanic *baunō (“bean”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰabʰ- (“bean”).
Cognate with Scots bene, bein (“bean”), North Frisian buan, Saterland Frisian Boone, West Frisian bean, beanne, Dutch boon, German Bohne, Luxembourgish Boun, Danish bønne, Faroese bøn, bøna, Icelandic baun, Norwegian Bokmål bønne, Norwegian Nynorsk bauna, baune, bogna

ex.en: Brazil supplies the world with coffee beans of quality.
ex.ja: ブラジルは世界に良質のコーヒー豆を供給しています。

ex.en: The man returned from his vacation full of beans.
ex.ja: その男は元気いっぱい、休暇から戻ってきた。

ex.en: I want to eat rice with beans.
ex.ja: 豆ご飯が食べたいな。

note.ja: 古英語 bēan から。「豆」。

en: Free from writing, printing, or marks; having an empty space to be filled in.
Lacking characteristics which give variety; uniform.
The white spot in the centre of a target; hence (figuratively) the object to which anything is directed or aimed, the range of such aim.
A lot by which nothing is gained; a ticket in a lottery on which no prize is indicated.
To make void; to erase.
To render ineffective by blanketing with turbulent airflow, such as from aircraft wake or reverse thrust.

blank.ety: From Middle English blank, blonc, blaunc, blaunche, from Anglo-Norman blonc, blaunc, blaunche, from Old French blanc, feminine blanche, from Frankish *blank (“gleaming, white, blinding”), from Proto-Germanic *blankaz (“white, bright, blinding”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleyǵ- (“to shine”). Akin to Old High German blanch (“shining, bright, white”) (German blank), Old English blanc (“white, grey”), blanca (“white steed”), Spanish blanco. More at blink, blind, blanch. Doublet of blanc.

ex.en: Fill in the blanks with suitable words.
ex.ja: 空所を適当な言葉でうめなさい。

ex.en: You must fill the blanks in with a pen.
ex.ja: ペンで空所に書き込まなければなりません。

ex.en: My memory is blank on the subject.
ex.ja: その問題では記憶がぜんぜんない。

note.ja: 古フランス語 blanc（白い）から。「白い」→「白紙の・空白の」。blanket（白い毛布）と同じ。

en: An animal from the subtribe Bubalina, also known as true buffalos, such as the Cape buffalo, Syncerus caffer, or the water buffalo, Bubal…
A related North American animal, the American bison, Bison bison.
To hunt buffalo.

buffalo.ety: Borrowed from Portuguese or Spanish búfalo (“buffalo”), from Late Latin būfalus, from Latin būbalus, from Ancient Greek βούβαλος (boúbalos, “antelope, wild ox”). Doublet of bubale and buffle.

ex.en: Hundreds of buffaloes moved toward the lake.
ex.ja: 何百というバッファローが湖のほうへ移動した。

ex.en: Is that a cow or a buffalo?
ex.ja: あれは牛ですか水牛ですか。

ex.en: A buffalo is akin to an ox.
ex.ja: 水牛は牛に似ている。

note.ja: ポルトガル語 búfalo から。ギリシャ語 boubalos（レイヨウ）。bous（牛）と同系。

en: A firmly held belief.
A judgement of guilt in a court of law.

conviction.ety: From late Middle English conviction, from Anglo-Norman conviction, from Latin convictiō, from convictus, the past participle of convincō (“to convict”). Equivalent to convict + -ion.

ex.en: It is hard to live up to your convictions.
ex.ja: 信念にしたがって行動するのは難しい。

ex.en: She always stands up for her convictions.
ex.ja: 彼女は常に自分の信念を弁護している。

ex.en: His words carry little conviction.
ex.ja: 彼の言葉は説得力がほとんどない。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ vict（打ち勝つ）+ ion。完全に打ち負かされて納得すること →「確信」、法廷で打ち負かすこと →「有罪判決」。

en: Willing to act dishonestly for personal gain; accepting bribes.
In a depraved state; debased; perverted; morally degenerate; weak in morals.
To make corrupt; to change from good to bad; to draw away from the right path; to deprave; to pervert.
To introduce errors; to place into an invalid state.

corrupt.ety: From Middle English corrupten, derived from Latin corruptus, past participle of corrumpō (“to destroy, ruin, injure, spoil, corrupt, bribe”), from com- (“together”) + rumpō (“to break in pieces”).

ex.en: Dan discovered that Matt was a corrupt cop.
ex.ja: ダンはマットが汚職警官であることに気付いた。

ex.en: That organization is corrupt to the core.
ex.ja: あの組織は芯まで、腐っている。

ex.en: That organization is corrupt to its core.
ex.ja: あの組織は芯まで、腐っている。

note.ja: cor（完全に）+ rupt（壊す）。すっかり壊れた →「腐敗した・堕落させる」。

en: An adult female of the species Bos taurus, especially one that has calved.
Any member of the species Bos taurus that is not of a bucking breed or fighting breed, regardless of sex or age, including steers and cal…
To intimidate; to daunt the spirits or courage of.

cow.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *gʷṓws
Proto-Germanic *kōz
Proto-West Germanic *kō
Old English cū
Middle English cow
English cow
Inherited from Middle English cow, cou, from Old English cū (“cow”), from Proto-West Germanic *kō, from Proto-Germanic *kōz (“cow”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷṓws (“cow”).
Cognate with Sanskrit गो (go), Ancient Greek βοῦς (boûs), Persian گاو (gâv)), Latvian govs (“cow”), Proto-Slavic *govędo (Serbo-Croatian govedo, Russian говядина (govjadina, “beef”), Scots coo (“cow”), North Frisian ko, kø (“cow”), West Frisian ko (“cow”), Dutch koe (“cow”), Low German Koh, Ko

ex.en: Cows supply us with many things we need.
ex.ja: 牛は私達に必要なものをたくさん与えてくれる。

ex.en: You can wait till the cows come home.
ex.ja: いつまででも待つがいいさ。

ex.en: He looked at the cows in the fields.
ex.ja: 彼は野原にいる牛を見ました。

note.ja: 古英語 cū から。ラテン語 bos と同じ祖先。食肉の beef はフランス語から。

en: A bend, such as in a road.
A simple figure containing no straight portions and no angles; a curved line.
To bend; to crook.
To cause to swerve from a straight course.

curve.ety: Attested since the 1690s, from Latin curvus (“bent, curved”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to bend, curve, turn”) + *-wós. Doublet of curb, shrink, carcer, and cancer.

ex.en: The boy knows how to throw a curve.
ex.ja: その少年はカーブの投げ方を知っている。

ex.en: It's a long road with no curves.
ex.ja: 曲り角のないのは長い道である。

ex.en: The road curves to the left around the building.
ex.ja: 道路はその建物のところで左にカーブしている。

note.ja: ラテン語 curvus（曲がった）から。「曲線」。

en: To press down.
To make depressed, sad or bored.

depress.ety: From Middle English depressen, from Old French depresser, from Latin dēpressus, perfect participle of dēprimō (“to press down, to weigh down”), from dē- (“off, away, down, out”) + premō (“to press”).

ex.en: I can't believe that he is that depressed.
ex.ja: 彼がそれほど落ち込んでいるとは思えないな。

ex.en: Tom is depressed because his girlfriend left him.
ex.ja: トムは彼女にふられて落ち込んでいる。

ex.en: Rain doesn't depress people who like reading.
ex.ja: 雨が降っても読書の好きな人は気がめいらない。

note.ja: de（下へ）+ press（押す）。押し下げる →「落ち込ませる・不景気にする」。

en: Eating dinner as a social function.
Entertaining someone to dinner.

ex.en: What do you say to dining out together?
ex.ja: 一緒に食事に出かけませんか。

ex.en: What do you say to dining out tonight?
ex.ja: 今夜外で食事をしませんか。

ex.en: She kept the dining room warm in winter.
ex.ja: 彼女は冬に食堂を暖かくしておいた。

note.ja: dine（食事をする）+ -ing。dine は古フランス語 disner、dinner と同じ。
